# Upper Savannah assessment geography and native map operation

This source edition puts all 87 listed monitoring sites and all 101 pollutant-specific cause rows from the 2026 draft SCDES assessment into the existing Upper Savannah scientific workspace. It retains the original 12-file assessment package and adds the complete station geography, scalar GIS attributes, original location-source responses, and an executable native map operation.

## What is included

The location set contains 67 WQP points in EPSG:4326, six WQP points in EPSG:4269, and 14 SCDES service points in EPSG:26917. All 87 station IDs match the draft listing. The last 14 source points are the original fish/biological monitoring records that did not have usable WQP location pages. Their full original service response and layer schema are included.

Each point has scalar fields for site, listed HUC12, county, description, impaired uses, listed causes, cause-specific priority text, RFP-focus membership, Eighteenmile membership, nutrient listing, original coordinate reference system and coordinate source. There is one integer flag per listed cause. Exact filters such as {"cause_tn":1}, {"listed_huc12":"030601020507"}, or {"site":"SV-268"} work with the existing native vector reader.

The four RFP focus HUC12s are 030601010703 (RS-24163), 030601010704 (RL-01020), 030601020502 (SV-790), and 030601020507 (SV-234). The current native SCDES point for SV-234 is in the NAD83 / UTM zone17N source layer, OBJECTID1966. Its full source attributes and original geometry remain available.

The assessment companions retain the draft listing, draft TMDL coverage, July28 2026 use-support snapshot, waters of concern, delistings, Hartwell priority facts, four source-field differences, original six-point intake, source catalog and model interpretation. The original companion hashes are unchanged.

## Coordinate handling

The three point files use native OGR GeoJSON with an explicit CRS member. The six EPSG:4269 points retain their original NAD83 coordinates; the 14 EPSG:26917 points retain their original projected x/y. The native review program verifies the actual Fiona/OGR CRS against the manifest before it saves a view. It uses the existing SpatialReview and pyproj transformations for the EPSG:5070 display and native watershed point queries.

The SCDES service also publishes latitude/longitude attributes. Those degree attributes are preserved inside each full original metadata record. Geometry uses the explicitly declared projected point coordinates, so there is no inferred degree-datum conversion. All 14 source records identify collection METHOD=Manual and TIER=4; these original fields are retained.

Original coordinate strings and original metadata descriptions remain separately available. The 2026 assessment description is a different field from the WQP or SCDES location description. That preserves differences between program editions without silently rewriting either source.

## Native operation

Materialize the full capsule under a working delivery directory, then use the current complete application and its populated scientific workspace:

    /opt/pyvenv/bin/python assessment/operate_assessment_maps.py --app-root /actual/current/upstate_forever_2026 --workspace /actual/populated/workspace

If the current project has no Workspace manifest yet, choose the project's shared Workspace path and add --create-workspace. This uses the original Workspace initializer and imports the actual assessment sources immediately; it preserves an existing Workspace at that path. Add --domain-manifest /actual/retained/domain/sources.json to import the retained original217-feature domain through the same source intake before its exact geometry is discovered. Repeated domain-manifest arguments retain additional original source editions. An already-imported domain can be selected from the current catalog without importing it again.

The source directory defaults to the script's own assessment directory. The program calls the original Workspace.import_sources method using geography-model-sources.json. The three primary vector entries and every retained companion become ordinary native source editions. The existing map viewer catalogs them automatically.

The operation creates eight saved review families:

- All listed monitoring sites across the current regional domain.
- One review for each of the four RFP focus HUC12s.
- Eighteenmile Creek assessment and nutrient context.
- The listed nitrogen/phosphorus sites.
- The two sites with differing source HUC labels, RS-06190 and SV-192.

It calls the maintained SpatialExports API for each saved view. The existing exporter produces its original PDF, SVG, PNG, source/provenance, overlay-feature and annotation members, together with the source/application archive and map pack. Letter paper and 220 dpi are defaults; --paper a4 and --dpi 150/220/300 select the existing alternatives. --skip-export retains the native saved views when a receiver is operating only the map workspace.

The original 217-feature Esri model domain is discovered by its decoded SHA256, 2300d9b32a513d70503222a5d2e782e032107297214036a58e8b444a312169af. Its original HUC12 field drives focus filters. Additional or successor domain layers can be supplied with repeated --domain-layer-id values from the real workspace catalog. Selected domain fields and original identities accompany every join.

The program inspects every station through the actual native point API, with zero query tolerance in the station's original CRS. For each selected watershed layer it keeps every polygon cover, original attributes, original feature identity and source SHA. The CSV preserves overlapping boundary matches and stations outside a particular retained domain. The original source geometry stays in the immutable workspace source, accessible through the native viewer; batch outputs keep its identity and attributes without duplicating the same full polygon geometry for each nearby station.

native-assessment-review/operation.json records the actual project, collection, saved-review and map-pack results. Additional source imports record the role, original manifest path, manifest SHA256 and actual source-collection ID. It is updated after each saved review and export so an interrupted worker can resume the same content-identified native operation. point-inspections.json and station-domain-joins.csv carry the operated station/domain results.

## Original study and discharge context

Supply each retained 2023 lake-study or wastewater-outfall source manifest with --context-manifest /actual/retained/context/sources.json. The operation imports the ordinary native edition and includes its vector layers automatically. Repeated context-manifest arguments combine both source editions in the same run. Existing context vector layers can also be selected by their real IDs with --context-layer-id. The program uses the existing native geometry query to include each source where it intersects a saved viewport, keeping its original attributes and provenance in the map pack. This joins the measured study and source-load work to the same assessment views.

## Combining completed model runs

The same saved views can include actual completed baseline and alternative raster layers:

    /opt/pyvenv/bin/python assessment/operate_assessment_maps.py --app-root /actual/current/upstate_forever_2026 --workspace /actual/populated/workspace --primary-layer-id ACTUAL_BASELINE_LAYER_ID --comparison-layer-id ACTUAL_ALTERNATIVE_LAYER_ID --mode difference

Layer IDs come from the maintained native catalog. The existing spatial engine checks the selected bands, grids and physical units. Its difference direction is alternative minus baseline. Workspace NDR/SDR mass rasters have already been converted from their original per-hectare outputs using the real cell area; the map operation performs no additional area multiplication.

## Reading the science

The listed HUC12 is the agency's station-context label. The native join records where the original point falls in the selected original polygons and keeps reporting/upstream fields. These source relationships support map interpretation and catchment work. Annual modeled exports are compared with relevant observed loads and periods through the existing scientific workflow.

Eighteenmile's HUC10 is 0306010106. The two component HUC12s are 030601010601 and 030601010602. The 2023 original report prints these as 03060101-06, 03060101-06-01 and 03060101-06-02. The four current listed stations in those two subwatersheds are SV-241, SV-376, SV-233 and SV-268. SV-268's TN/TP priority1 and turbidity priority3 remain separate. The full 2023 lake study has its own station, seasonal concentration, physical and monthly measurement companions.

## Original sources

- SCDES current draft 2026 Integrated Report: https://apps.des.sc.gov/PublicNotices/SearchAndDisplay/PDF/302110 . The regional listing is on physical PDF pages 67-71.
- SCDES TMDL use support, July28 2026: https://des.sc.gov/sites/des/files/Documents/BOW/WaterQuality/TMDLAttainmentStatus.pdf .
- WQP station metadata: individual original URLs are retained for all 73 sites in station_metadata_20261013.json.
- SCDES station layer: https://gis.des.sc.gov/gisserver/rest/services/water/BW_Monitoring_Stations/MapServer/9 . The complete layer metadata and exact 14-site response are included.
- Publisher route to the live station application: https://des.sc.gov/programs/bureau-water/watersheds-program/sc-watershed-atlas and https://gis.des.sc.gov/gisportal/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=d0827cf30d3c490f9e22dd1000b8195a .
- Original 2023 Eighteenmile lake study: https://des.sc.gov/sites/des/files/Documents/BOW/WaterQuality/2023LakeProgramFinalReport.pdf .

# Upper Savannah assessment and model interpretation

Operation: ECOSYSTEM-SCIENCES-ASSESSMENT-20261013  
Prepared: 2026-10-13

This package supplies the existing Upper Savannah application with current, pollutant-specific assessment records and original monitoring locations. It joins the four RFP focus watersheds to the broader connected model domain and identifies a directly relevant nitrogen/phosphorus priority at the Eighteen Mile Creek arm of Lake Hartwell.

## Source editions and coverage

The [2026 draft Integrated Report](https://apps.des.sc.gov/PublicNotices/SearchAndDisplay/PDF/302110) contains the current draft listing and appendices. Its [public notice](https://apps.des.sc.gov/PublicNotices/SearchAndDisplay/Display/38165) runs through October 15, 2026. The updated assessment uses 2020-2024 data; previously listed conditions can carry forward when recent data are unavailable. Preserve the draft edition in map labels and exports.

The separately published [TMDL use-support table](https://des.sc.gov/sites/des/files/Documents/BOW/WaterQuality/TMDLAttainmentStatus.pdf) is dated July 28, 2026. These two editions are represented independently so a station can have an approved bacteria TMDL, a dated recreation attainment result, and a different current listed cause.

The extracted candidate region is HUC8 03060101, 03060102 and 03060103. Join its 12-digit HUC strings to the original 217-HUC12 domain before reporting domain counts. Preserve the original 116 reporting intersections and 101 upstream ancestors, the separate Upper Savannah reporting mask, and the buffered model grid.

## Delivered records

- 101 listed site/use/cause rows across 87 monitoring sites, including the original station descriptions and source-row use/cause/priority values.
- 70 approved-TMDL coverage rows from the draft report.
- 68 dated TMDL use-support rows: 65 Not Supported and three Fully Supported for recreation/E. coli. The three are SV-206, SV-015 and SV-139; other uses and causes retain their own status.
- 10 waters-of-concern changes and three pollutant-specific delistings.
- Three Hartwell priority/context records and seven model interpretation profiles.
- Six original WQP monitoring locations in CSV and GeoJSON.
- Four published source-field differences, with original-report resolutions or original coordinates for spatial resolution.

All source pages are one-based physical PDF pages. SOURCES.json records original URLs, editions, extraction pages, dictionaries and counts. HUC identifiers must remain strings to preserve leading zeroes.

## Focus watersheds and model questions

| HUC12 | Station | Current draft concern | Application use |
|---|---|---|---|
| 030601010703 | RS-24163 | Recreation / E. coli, priority 3 | Catchment management context; retain bacteria observations separately |
| 030601010704 | RL-01020 | Aquatic life / pH, priority 3 | Nutrient-pressure context alongside dated pH direction and conditions |
| 030601020502 | SV-790 | Aquatic life / macroinvertebrates, priority 3 | Connected sediment and nutrient pressure screening |
| 030601020507 | SV-234 | Fish consumption / PCB, priority 3 | Upland sediment-management context with fish-tissue assessment |
| 030601010602 | SV-268 | Aquatic life / TN and TP, priority 1; turbidity, priority 3 | Direct annual nutrient-export scenario comparison; sediment-source context |

Priority 1 represents agency planning for 2026-2028, priority 2 for 2028-2030, and priority 3 after 2030. It is an assessment planning field. Keep all four RFP focus watersheds in the delivery.

At SV-268, the TN/TP listing, turbidity listing, pH protection context, lead water-of-concern record and legacy fecal-coliform TMDL are separate facts. The Appendix E pH standard-attained comment applies to pH. The annual nutrient profiles connect to NDR nitrogen and phosphorus export.

## Map and observation integration

Render verified station points from observed_monitoring_sites.geojson using longitude/latitude in WGS84. Keep the provider-qualified monitoring_location_id for original-data joins. Station metadata reports nutrient-record start/end years; a date range does not establish measurements in every year.

Use the HUC polygon label "Contains listed monitoring site." Retain the modeled contributing area as its own spatial relationship. A station's listed cause does not classify every location in its HUC polygon. The separate DES water-classification reach layer carries its own source attributes.

RS-06190 has published HUC12 values 030601030602 and 030601030502; SV-192 has 030601030513 and 030601030613. Both original points are supplied for a point-in-polygon join against the retained original HUC geometry. Preserve the published values in source_field_differences.csv and write a distinct derived spatial HUC field. The native observation owner already has the six-point join request in the project thread. SV-234 remains keyed to its published station/HUC relationship while its original fish-tissue coordinate source is recovered.

## Model units, comparison direction and use

The [InVEST 3.20 NDR guide](https://storage.googleapis.com/releases.naturalcapitalproject.org/invest/3.20.0/userguide/en/ndr.html) and [SDR guide](https://storage.googleapis.com/releases.naturalcapitalproject.org/invest/3.20.0/userguide/en/sdr.html) define the native outputs. Raw NDR rasters n_total_export and p_surface_export are kg/ha/year; raw SDR sed_export is metric tonnes/ha/year.

The retained application converts these raw rates once through model.rasters.rate_to_mass. Its workspace nitrogen_export, phosphorus_export and sediment_export rasters are already annual mass per pixel. Sum those workspace values directly over their retained support. A raw 30 m rate cell uses 0.09 ha exactly once; native watershed summaries are already annual mass.

The native comparison is alternative minus baseline. A display called "reduction" uses baseline minus alternative, the negative of that native difference. Retain the calculation direction in exports.

Compare modeled annual exports to source-calculated annual loads for the matching contributing area, period, parameter and units through model.observations. Use concentration, bacteria, pH, biological, fish-tissue and turbidity observations as their respective measured context. Reservoir comparisons need a named contributing area and explicit treatment of reservoir retention. SDR represents upland sheet/rill erosion; the sediment profile retains that physical scope.

## Assessment updates and source reconciliation

The agency removed affected pH readings from its Appalachia II office for August 1, 2022 through July 31, 2023 from the 2026 assessment and WQP. The supplied waters-of-concern table carries the resulting site-specific statuses, including six pH records now NOT IMPAIRED and SV-236 now IMPAIRED.

Original reports resolve two reference differences: [Cane/Little Cane report 017-05](https://des.sc.gov/sites/des/files/docs/HomeAndEnvironment/Docs/tmdl_cane2.pdf) is dated May 2005, supporting 2005 for SV-832; [Upper Savannah report 026-05](https://des.sc.gov/sites/des/files/docs/HomeAndEnvironment/Docs/tmdl_upsav_fc.pdf) is dated July 2005 and the July 2026 site table binds SV-735 to that report. Source values stay intact alongside the preferred references.

The draft coverage table adds RS-24122 and RS-24119 relative to the dated July table. Join by station, use, pollutant, source edition and assessment date; retain the legacy fecal-coliform marker on July E. coli attainment records.

## Installation

Materialize the complete capsule from its Slack Canvas into the existing Upper Savannah product root. The verified decoder writes the assessment/ files using the application's atomic writer. The GeoJSON, fact CSVs and model companion then join the existing assessment overlay, observation comparison and report/export paths. They require no replacement runner or new model source acquisition.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compose editable GIS with the maintained Operator; preserve unrelated source edits."""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import tempfile

MODEL_FILES = ('gis_project.py', 'gis_workspace.py', 'gis_project_cli.py',
               'gis_project_native.py', 'gis_project_view.html', 'GIS_PROJECTS.md', 'requirements-gis.txt')
OWN_FILES = tuple('model/' + x for x in MODEL_FILES) + (
    'operator/gis_projects.py', 'operator/web/gis-projects.mjs', 'operator/web/gis-projects.css',
    'operator/extensions/gis-projects.json')
MARKER = '# Editable GIS integration: ASTRA-GIS12/v1'


def sha(body):
    return hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()


def once(text, old, new, label):
    if text.count(old) != 1:
        raise ValueError('Original source seam differs: ' + label + '. Compose against its current owner revision.')
    return text.replace(old, new, 1)


def server_source(text):
    if MARKER in text:
        return text
    text = once(text, 'class Operator:', MARKER + '\nfrom gis_projects import ACTIONS as GIS_ACTIONS, GISProjects\nACTIONS = set(ACTIONS) | GIS_ACTIONS\n\nclass Operator:', 'Operator declaration')
    # Select _invoke structurally; other extensions can use their own action local.
    tree = ast.parse(text)
    cls = next(x for x in tree.body if isinstance(x, ast.ClassDef) and x.name == 'Operator')
    fn = next(x for x in cls.body if isinstance(x, ast.FunctionDef) and x.name == '_invoke')
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    body = ''.join(lines[fn.lineno - 1:fn.end_lineno])
    body = once(body, '        action = task["action"]\n', '        action = task["action"]\n        if action in GIS_ACTIONS:\n            return GISProjects(self).invoke(task)\n', '_invoke action')
    text = ''.join(lines[:fn.lineno - 1]) + body + ''.join(lines[fn.end_lineno:])
    # Existing review/task decorators remain the terminal writer.
    text = once(text, '        return self.customer_reviews.decorate_task(task)',
                '        task = GISProjects(self).decorate_task(task)\n        return self.customer_reviews.decorate_task(task)', 'task_view decorator')
    old = '            if url.path.startswith("/api/file/"):\n'
    new = '''            if url.path.startswith("/api/file/gis-project/"):
                self.authorized(file=True)
                parts = url.path.removeprefix("/api/file/gis-project/").split("/", 3)
                if len(parts) != 4:
                    raise ValueError("Choose an original GIS project member")
                ticket, policy = GISProjects(self.app).member(*[urllib.parse.unquote(x) for x in parts])
                return self.send_file(ticket["id"], download=one("download") == "1", content_security_policy=policy)
'''+old
    text = once(text, old, new, 'original file routing')
    old = '                workspace = one("workspace", self.app.primary)\n'
    text = once(text, old, old + '                if url.path == "/api/gis/projects":\n                    return self.send_json(200, GISProjects(self.app).catalogue(workspace))\n', 'original authorized GET workspace')
    tree = ast.parse(text)
    selected = [n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.Compare) and
                isinstance(n.left, ast.Name) and n.left.id == 'selected' and
                len(n.ops) == 1 and isinstance(n.ops[0], ast.NotIn) and
                isinstance(n.comparators[0], ast.Set) and
                any(isinstance(e, ast.Constant) and e.value == 'app.mjs' for e in n.comparators[0].elts)]
    if len(selected) != 1:
        raise ValueError('Original browser asset admission changed')
    node = selected[0].comparators[0]
    rows = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    before = sum(len(x.encode('utf-8')) for x in rows[:node.end_lineno - 1]) + node.end_col_offset - 1
    raw = text.encode('utf-8')
    text = (raw[:before] + b', "gis-projects.mjs", "gis-projects.css"' + raw[before:]).decode('utf-8')
    ast.parse(text)
    return text


def browser_source(text):
    if "import {attachGISProjects}" in text:
        return text
    text = "import {attachGISProjects} from './gis-projects.mjs';\n" + text
    text = once(text, 'const viewLabels={', "const viewLabels={'gis-projects':'Editable GIS projects',", 'view names')
    text = once(text, 'const actionLabels={', "const actionLabels={'gis.project.export':'Build editable GIS project','gis.project.receive':'Receive editable GIS project','gis.project.adopt-sources':'Adopt received GIS sources',", 'action names')
    text = once(text, 'function toast(message){', "const gisProjects=attachGISProjects({getState:()=>state,api,refreshState:refresh,showTask,toast});\nfunction toast(message){", 'original UI factory')
    text = once(text, '    renderTasks();\n', '    renderTasks();\n    gisProjects.update(data);\n', 'retained state refresh')
    seam="  if(view==='spatial'){"
    text = once(text, seam, "  if(view==='gis-projects'){community.detach();customerReviews.detach();spatialWorkspace.suspend();gisProjects.mount($('#content'),state);return;}\n  gisProjects.detach();\n" + seam, 'original view lifecycle')
    return text


def index_source(text):
    if 'data-view="gis-projects"' in text:
        return text
    seam='<link rel="stylesheet" href="/web/reviews.css">'
    text=once(text,seam,seam+'\n  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/web/gis-projects.css">','original stylesheet list')
    seam='<button data-view="runs">Native model runs</button>'
    return once(text,seam,seam+'\n    <button data-view="gis-projects">Editable GIS projects</button>','original navigation')



def legacy_server_source(text):
    """Remove only the exact former GIS-owned joins before shared registration."""
    if MARKER not in text:
        return text
    text = once(text, MARKER + '\nfrom gis_projects import ACTIONS as GIS_ACTIONS, GISProjects\nACTIONS = set(ACTIONS) | GIS_ACTIONS\n\n', '', 'legacy GIS provider')
    text = once(text, '        if action in GIS_ACTIONS:\n            return GISProjects(self).invoke(task)\n', '', 'legacy GIS dispatch')
    text = once(text, '        task = GISProjects(self).decorate_task(task)\n', '', 'legacy GIS task decoration')
    text = once(text, '''            if url.path.startswith("/api/file/gis-project/"):
                self.authorized(file=True)
                parts = url.path.removeprefix("/api/file/gis-project/").split("/", 3)
                if len(parts) != 4:
                    raise ValueError("Choose an original GIS project member")
                ticket, policy = GISProjects(self.app).member(*[urllib.parse.unquote(x) for x in parts])
                return self.send_file(ticket["id"], download=one("download") == "1", content_security_policy=policy)
''', '', 'legacy GIS file route')
    text = once(text, '                if url.path == "/api/gis/projects":\n                    return self.send_json(200, GISProjects(self.app).catalogue(workspace))\n', '', 'legacy GIS catalogue')
    return once(text, ', "gis-projects.mjs", "gis-projects.css"', '', 'legacy GIS static assets')


def legacy_browser_source(text):
    if "import {attachGISProjects}" not in text:
        return text
    labels = (
        "const actionLabels={'gis.project.export':'Build editable GIS project','gis.project.receive':'Receive editable GIS project','gis.project.adopt-sources':'Adopt received GIS sources',",
        "const actionLabels={'gis.project.export':'Build editable GIS project','gis.project.receive':'Receive editable GIS project',",
    )
    old_labels = next((value for value in labels if value in text), None)
    if old_labels is None:
        raise ValueError('Compose the current GIS action labels before shared registration')
    for old, new, label in (
        ("import {attachGISProjects} from './gis-projects.mjs';\n", '', 'legacy GIS import'),
        ("const viewLabels={'gis-projects':'Editable GIS projects',", 'const viewLabels={', 'legacy GIS view'),
        (old_labels, 'const actionLabels={', 'legacy GIS actions'),
        ("const gisProjects=attachGISProjects({getState:()=>state,api,refreshState:refresh,showTask,toast});\n", '', 'legacy GIS controller'),
        ('    gisProjects.update(data);\n', '', 'legacy GIS refresh'),
        ("  if(view==='gis-projects'){community.detach();customerReviews.detach();spatialWorkspace.suspend();gisProjects.mount($('#content'),state);return;}\n  gisProjects.detach();\n", '', 'legacy GIS lifecycle'),
    ):
        text = once(text, old, new, label)
    return text


def legacy_index_source(text):
    for old in ('\n  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/web/gis-projects.css">',
                '\n    <button data-view="gis-projects">Editable GIS projects</button>'):
        if old in text:
            text = once(text, old, '', 'legacy GIS navigation or stylesheet')
    return text


def registration_plan(application):
    """Use the receiving application's maintained host, with one active GIS owner."""
    host = application / 'install_extensions.py'
    if not host.is_file():
        return ({'operator/server.py': server_source,
                 'operator/web/app.mjs': browser_source,
                 'operator/web/index.html': index_source}, None, 'legacy')
    if host.is_symlink():
        raise ValueError('The maintained extension installer is a symbolic link')
    registry = application / 'operator/extension_registry.py'
    if not registry.is_file():
        raise ValueError('Receive the current complete extension host with install_extensions.py')
    registry_body = registry.read_bytes()
    if b'def file_reply(' not in registry_body or b'def _member_path(' not in registry_body:
        raise ValueError('Receive the maintained extension host with nested member file routes')
    body = host.read_bytes()
    # This is an installed application module, never source supplied by a GIS ZIP.
    namespace = {'__name__': '_upstate_gis_current_extension_installer', '__file__': str(host)}
    exec(compile(body, str(host), 'exec'), namespace)
    if not callable(namespace.get('patch_server')) or not callable(namespace.get('patch_app')):
        raise ValueError('The current extension installer lacks its source composition API')
    transform = {
        'operator/server.py': lambda value: namespace['patch_server'](legacy_server_source(value)),
        'operator/web/app.mjs': lambda value: namespace['patch_app'](legacy_browser_source(value)),
        'operator/web/index.html': legacy_index_source,
    }
    return transform, {host: body, registry: registry_body}, 'registry'


def install(application, source, dry_run=False):
    application, source = Path(application).resolve(strict=True), Path(source).resolve(strict=True)
    if not (application / 'model/workspace.py').is_file():
        raise ValueError('Receive the original scientific application before this additive component')
    transform, dependencies, integration = registration_plan(application)
    before={};planned={}
    for name, fn in transform.items():
        path=application/name
        if path.is_symlink(): raise ValueError('Original registration file is a symbolic link')
        before[name]=path.read_bytes();planned[name]=fn(before[name].decode('utf-8')).encode('utf-8')
    for name in OWN_FILES:
        data=(source/name).read_bytes();target=application/name
        if target.is_symlink(): raise ValueError('Component destination is a symbolic link')
        before[name]=target.read_bytes() if target.exists() else None
        # This installer is intentionally the owner of these named additive files.
        planned[name]=data
    for name, data in planned.items():
        if name.endswith('.py'): compile(data,str(application/name),'exec')
    changes=[name for name in planned if planned[name]!=before[name]]
    result={'schema':'upstate.gis-installation/v1','application':str(application),'dry_run':dry_run,
            'integration':integration,
            'files':[{'path':name,'before_sha256':sha(before[name]) if before[name] is not None else None,
                      'sha256':sha(planned[name]),'bytes':len(planned[name])} for name in changes]}
    if dry_run or not changes:return result
    # A shared original owner can inspect/undo exact registration edits from this journal.
    journal=application/'source_tools'/'gis-installations'
    journal.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    operation=sha(json.dumps(result,sort_keys=True).encode())
    record=journal/(operation+'.json')
    staged={};applied=[]
    try:
        for name in changes:
            path=application/name;path.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=path.parent,prefix='.gis-install-',delete=False) as out:
                out.write(planned[name]);out.flush();os.fsync(out.fileno());staged[name]=Path(out.name)
        # Compare all predecessors immediately before committing any registration changes.
        for dependency, expected in (dependencies or {}).items():
            if dependency.read_bytes() != expected:
                raise ValueError('Concurrent extension host change: ' + str(dependency))
        for name in changes:
            p=application/name
            actual=p.read_bytes() if p.exists() else None
            if actual!=before[name]:raise ValueError('Concurrent original source change: '+name)
        for name in changes:
            p=application/name
            actual=p.read_bytes() if p.exists() else None
            if actual!=before[name]:raise ValueError('Concurrent original source change: '+name)
            if before[name] is not None:
                backup=journal/(operation+'-'+name.replace('/','__')+'.before')
                backup.write_bytes(before[name])
            os.replace(staged[name],p);applied.append(name)
        record.write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n',encoding='utf-8')
    except BaseException:
        for name in reversed(applied):
            p=application/name
            if p.read_bytes()!=planned[name]:continue
            if before[name] is None:p.unlink()
            else:
                with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=p.parent,prefix='.gis-rollback-',delete=False) as out:
                    out.write(before[name]);out.flush();os.fsync(out.fileno());temporary=Path(out.name)
                os.replace(temporary,p)
        raise
    finally:
        for p in staged.values():p.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return result


def main():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument('--application',required=True)
    p.add_argument('--source-root',default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    p.add_argument('--dry-run',action='store_true')
    args=p.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(install(args.application,args.source_root,args.dry_run),indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Install the published-study desk into the existing ECSA application."""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone

CODE_FILES = (
    "measurement_workspace/published_studies.py",
    "measurement_workspace/observation_support.py",
    "measurement_workspace/OBSERVATION_SUPPORT.md",
    "operator/published_study_operator.py",
    "operator/extensions/published-studies.json",
    "operator/web/published_studies.mjs",
    "operator/web/published_studies.css",
    "PUBLISHED_STUDIES.md",
    "install_published_studies.py",
    "receive_published_studies.py",
    "tools/attach_published_report.py",
)
DATA_ROOT = Path("observations/eighteenmile_2023")


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def atomic_copy(source, target):
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="." + target.name + "-", dir=target.parent)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as output:
            output.write(source.read_bytes())
            output.flush()
            os.fsync(output.fileno())
        os.replace(temporary, target)
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(temporary):
            os.unlink(temporary)


def portable_source(source):
    """Extend the original archive inventory while preserving its other code."""
    additions = {
        "APPLICATION_DIRECTORIES": ("measurement_workspace", "observations"),
        "APPLICATION_FILES": (
            "PUBLISHED_STUDIES.md", "install_published_studies.py",
            "receive_published_studies.py", "tools/attach_published_report.py",
            "eighteenmile_chlorophyll_reconciled.sources.json",
            "eighteenmile_lake_observation_report.sources.json",
            "eighteenmile_lake_paired_analysis.sources.json",
        ),
    }
    lines = source.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets = [0]
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(offsets[-1] + len(line))
    replacements = []
    found = set()
    for node in ast.parse(source).body:
        if not isinstance(node, ast.Assign) or len(node.targets) != 1 or not isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name):
            continue
        name = node.targets[0].id
        if name not in additions:
            continue
        found.add(name)
        original = ast.literal_eval(node.value)
        if not isinstance(original, (list, tuple)) or any(not isinstance(item, str) for item in original):
            raise ValueError("The native archive inventory is not a literal filename list: " + name)
        updated = tuple(original) + tuple(item for item in additions[name] if item not in original)
        if tuple(original) != updated:
            start = offsets[node.value.lineno - 1] + node.value.col_offset
            end = offsets[node.value.end_lineno - 1] + node.value.end_col_offset
            replacements.append((start, end, repr(updated)))
    if found != set(additions):
        raise ValueError("The native portable module is missing its application inventory.")
    for start, end, replacement in sorted(replacements, reverse=True):
        source = source[:start] + replacement + source[end:]
    return source


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--application", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    source = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    application = Path(args.application).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)
    for required in ("model/workspace.py", "operator/extension_registry.py"):
        if not (application / required).is_file():
            parser.error("The existing ECSA application is missing " + required)
    data_files = [str(path.relative_to(source)) for path in sorted((source / DATA_ROOT).iterdir()) if path.is_file()]
    observations = source / DATA_ROOT / "wqp_20261013"
    if observations.is_dir():
        data_files.extend(str(path.relative_to(source)) for path in sorted(observations.iterdir()) if path.is_file())
    cohort = source / DATA_ROOT / "cohort_reconciliation_20261013"
    if cohort.is_dir():
        data_files.extend(str(path.relative_to(source)) for path in sorted(cohort.rglob("*")) if path.is_file())
    cohort_manifest = "eighteenmile_chlorophyll_reconciled.sources.json"
    if (source / cohort_manifest).is_file():
        data_files.append(cohort_manifest)
    for manifest in (
        source / DATA_ROOT / "model-sources.json",
        source / DATA_ROOT / "wqp" / "flow-context-sources.json",
        source / DATA_ROOT / "wqp" / "flow-context-public-sources.json",
        source / DATA_ROOT / "wqp_20261013" / "source-manifest.json",
        source / DATA_ROOT / "figures" / "model-sources.json",
        source / "eighteenmile_chlorophyll_reconciled.sources.json",
        source / "eighteenmile_lake_observation_report.sources.json",
        source / "eighteenmile_lake_paired_analysis.sources.json",
    ):
        if not manifest.is_file():
            continue
        value = json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
        if value.get("schema") != "upstate.sources/v1":
            parser.error("Incompatible installed source manifest: " + str(manifest))
        data_files.append(str(manifest.relative_to(source)))
        for entry in value.get("entries", []):
            for item in [entry, *entry.get("companions", [])]:
                path = (manifest.parent / item["path"]).resolve(strict=True)
                if not path.is_relative_to((source / DATA_ROOT).resolve()):
                    parser.error("A study manifest refers outside its source directory.")
                data_files.append(str(path.relative_to(source)))
    flow_manifest = DATA_ROOT / "wqp" / "flow-context-sources.json"
    if (source / flow_manifest).is_file():
        data_files.append(str(flow_manifest))
    support_result = DATA_ROOT / "microcystin_support_20261013" / "original-campaign-support.json"
    if (source / support_result).is_file():
        data_files.append(str(support_result))
    data_files = sorted(set(data_files))
    expected = list(CODE_FILES) + data_files
    for relative in expected:
        if not (source / relative).is_file():
            parser.error("The source carrier is missing " + relative)
    for relative in data_files:
        target = application / relative
        if target.exists() and digest(target) != digest(source / relative):
            parser.error("Published source bytes differ at " + str(target) + "; retain that edition separately before installing this companion.")
    portable_path = application / "model" / "portable.py"
    portable_original = portable_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    portable_updated = portable_source(portable_original)
    stamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    changed, reused = [], []
    for relative in expected:
        original, target = source / relative, application / relative
        if target.is_file() and digest(target) == digest(original):
            reused.append(relative)
            continue
        if target.exists():
            backup = application / ".published-studies-backups" / stamp / relative
            backup.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copy2(target, backup)
        atomic_copy(original, target)
        changed.append(relative)
    if portable_updated != portable_original:
        backup = application / ".published-studies-backups" / stamp / "model" / "portable.py"
        backup.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(portable_path, backup)
        fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".portable-", dir=portable_path.parent)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as output:
                output.write(portable_updated)
            os.replace(temporary, portable_path)
        finally:
            if os.path.exists(temporary):
                os.unlink(temporary)
        changed.append("model/portable.py")
    package = application / "measurement_workspace" / "__init__.py"
    if not package.exists():
        package.write_text('"""Measurement workspace extensions."""\n', encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({
        "schema": "upstate.published-study-install/v1",
        "application": str(application),
        "installed": changed, "reused": reused,
        "extension": "published-studies", "view": "published-studies",
        "action": "published-study.import",
        "builtin_id": "scdes-eighteenmile-lake-2023",
        "files": [{"path": name, "sha256": digest(application / name)} for name in expected],
    }, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Measurement workspace extensions."""

# Original concentration coverage in Published studies

This additive module enriches the existing study context with reporting-limit support. It leaves the original concentration values, source cohorts, printed table summaries, selected observations, quantified-only statistics and native model calculations intact.

## Scientific meaning

For each original station / parameter / source-project / activity-type series, a quantified result contributes its reported concentration. A result explicitly below a positive original reporting limit contributes the interval from zero to that limit, excluding the upper endpoint, conditional on nonnegative concentration. Divide the sum of those intervals by the complete result-row count.

These are arithmetic bounds on the mean of the retained observations, conditional on the original censor statements. They are not confidence intervals, estimates of a population mean, or assigned values for individual samples. No zero, half-limit or other point substitution is written into a source row. Missing/unsupported numerical support, a negative quantified concentration conflicting with the stated assumption, or incompatible units leaves the aggregate interval unavailable. Original qualifiers, activity counts, result identities and source selectors remain accessible.

The selected Eighteenmile source contains 85 microcystin results. The published Table 8 analytical summary contains 73 samples. Its printed statistics remain separate. Four April 5 original records use a 0.1 ug/L limit; the other relevant limits are 0.016 ug/L. Original methods and detection fields are retained in the result artifact.

## Existing native context integration

In measurement_workspace/published_studies.py, use the sibling module:

```python
from .observation_support import enrich_observation_context, report_html as support_report_html
```

In PublishedStudyStore.context, directly after the existing call to _observation_context(...):

```python
observation_context = enrich_observation_context(observation_context)
```

The selected-context JSON and existing study export then retain each series' observation_support object. This contains full numerical endpoints, complete original detection support and selected result/source IDs.

In PublishedStudyStore.report_html, append support_report_html(context) to the existing observed HTML before composing the final page. It renders two readable tables per original parameter/project/activity-type series: coverage and mean intervals. This uses the original report's industrial styling and small table widths.

Keep the concurrent report-manifest and flow-manifest traversal additions when applying these two hooks. No importer or source-manifest alteration is needed.

## Existing scientific report integration

The maintained observed_context collector can append:

```python
from measurement_workspace.observation_support import report_sections
sections.extend(report_sections(original_published_study_context))
```

The returned value matches the actual v6/v7 scientific report contract: a list of (heading, blocks) pairs; ordinary paragraphs are strings and table blocks use kind, columns, rows, widths and caption. Therefore the same values render in PDF, HTML, Markdown and structured report data. Preserve the existing observed source binding in the delivery identity.

## Existing native receiving continuation

On the same actual application and exported study context:

```sh
python -B -m measurement_workspace.observation_support /actual/selected-context.json --output /actual/observation-support
```

This command reads a native upstate.published-study-context/v1 export, writes its enriched selected-context.json, exact scientific report section JSON and complete original study-report.html with the new support section. It uses the maintained PublishedStudyStore HTML exporter.

Inspect the five actual microcystin series and original source links in that same report. The accompanying original-campaign-support.json contains source arithmetic evaluated directly from the complete original 920-result CSV and preserves every one of the 85 underlying microcystin records. The module's native execution belongs to the existing report receive operation.

Its four-part series key, source value/limit fields, record selectors and static report_html contract match this module. # Original-catchment calibration maps and editable GIS

This workflow connects a completed annual-load calibration to its actual upstream catchments. It creates registered vector sources, complete numeric tables, per-pollutant atlases and ordinary saved Spatial reviews. Those same sources enter the maintained editable GIS exporter without a new model runner or a separate map application.

Every figure and vector attribute derives from an existing completed calibration report. The workflow keeps the original selected candidate, observation edition, catchment IDs, source periods, calibration/validation split, normalization scales and native support. It can add the already saved published-source-error supplement.

## Operator workflow

Open the completed calibration, choose **Prepare original catchment maps**, and select the existing source-error supplement if needed. The default includes the original selected candidate. Additional eligible candidate runs can be included for calibration units only.

The resulting retained map edition provides:

- A source layer for every selected candidate/pollutant pair, with complete original catchment polygons and numeric residual attributes.
- A PDF atlas and scalable SVG pages for each layer.
- A CSV containing all plotted and inspectable values, original source-record IDs and periods.
- A printable HTML index linking the complete files.
- Original calibration, selection, observation-edition and source-CSV copies, plus source-error JSON when selected.
- Direct opening of each registered vector in the existing Spatial review.
- A saved Spatial review with solid calibration outlines and dashed held-out selected-candidate outlines.
- A ready selection for the original editable GIS export, including scientific context attachments.

The native Spatial review uses its maintained outline and point-attribute inspection controls. Its ordinary vector overlays are not described as a shaded residual raster. The separate atlas provides signed residual figures with grayscale magnitude.

The model API is:

```python
from model import calibration_maps

maps = calibration_maps.prepare(
    workspace,
    actual_completed_calibration_id,
    uncertainty_id=actual_retained_source_error_id,  # optional
    candidate_run_ids=actual_eligible_run_ids,       # optional; defaults to selected
)
maps = calibration_maps.inspect(workspace, maps["id"])
link = calibration_maps.save_review(workspace, maps["id"], maps["layers"][0]["id"])
```

Only existing IDs are accepted. Selected run ordering follows the original ranking, so changing checkbox order does not create a second edition. The original selected candidate must remain in the chosen cohort.

Command line, from the application root:

```sh
python -m model.calibration_maps /path/to/original/workspace prepare EXISTING_CALIBRATION_ID
python -m model.calibration_maps /path/to/original/workspace prepare EXISTING_CALIBRATION_ID --uncertainty-id EXISTING_UNCERTAINTY_ID
python -m model.calibration_maps /path/to/original/workspace inspect RETURNED_MAP_ID
python -m model.calibration_maps /path/to/original/workspace save-review RETURNED_MAP_ID EXISTING_LAYER_ID
```

Repeat `--candidate-run-id` for an explicit cohort, including the originally selected run. The action uses completed saved prediction rows; it does not execute InVEST or fit a new estimator.

## Original geometry and coordinate systems

The original calibration plan identifies its source collection, vector source, native layer, property filter and catchment identity field. The workflow reopens that exact retained source through `Workspace.source_file`, which verifies original bytes, hashes and companion relationships. Its primary body must match the catchment source recorded in the original calibration spatial grouping.

The original catchment identity field must remain unique and non-null. Every required calibration catchment must be present. A valid Polygon or MultiPolygon is required; invalid geometry receives an explicit exception rather than an automatic repair.

The maintained `rasters.vector_geometry` reader handles the original native vector source, including its gzip path support. All polygon components and interior rings remain present.

Two coordinate systems serve different purposes:

| Product | Coordinates |
| --- | --- |
| Registered GeoJSON | EPSG:4326 longitude/latitude, transformed from the original source with explicit x/y axis order |
| Atlas and saved review | The originally selected candidate's retained projected model-grid CRS in metres |
| Source provenance | Original source WKT, output CRS, actual atlas CRS and source body/companions |

The atlas projection comes from the original saved model grid; it is not an assumed statewide projection. Reprojection is checked for valid finite geometry. There is no union, simplification, clipping, rasterization or replacement catchment delineation.

## What one feature means

One feature represents one original catchment/pollutant reference unit for one selected completed candidate. The feature ID binds the original run ID and unit ID. The original catchment ID, source feature ID, station IDs, candidate/profile identity, parameter and native units remain scalar or JSON-text attributes.

The physical quantities are:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `observed_annual_mass` | Original saved time-weighted annual reference for this catchment/pollutant |
| `native_annual_mass` | Retained completed native catchment load |
| `delivered_external_annual_mass` | Original explicitly supplied delivered external load |
| `predicted_annual_mass` | The quantity used by the original calibration, including that external load |
| `residual` | Predicted annual load minus original annual reference |
| `absolute_residual` | Magnitude of that signed residual |
| `relative_residual_percent` | 100 × residual / reference, only when the original reference is positive |
| `normalized_residual` | Residual divided by the original retained pollutant normalization scale |

Nitrogen and phosphorus retain kg/year. Sediment retains metric tonnes/year. Each source layer and each atlas is specific to one pollutant. No cross-pollutant mass sum is supplied.

# Source-error sensitivity of the retained calibration

This module analyzes how the original completed calibration ranking changes inside declared bands around the original published annual-load estimates. It uses the saved native predictions, source observation edition, spatial split, temporal weights, external-load adjustments, pollutant weights and normalization scales. Results retain the original selected run and profile.

The output answers three concrete questions:

1. Does the selected candidate have a strictly smaller objective throughout the chosen source-error region?
2. Which completed challengers can tie or outperform it somewhere in that region, and which original source rows contribute to the change?
3. At what multiple of the published standard errors does each challenger first tie the selected candidate, accounting for the nonnegative-load boundary?

This is a deterministic supplement to an existing result. Its work is proportional to the saved candidate/reference table plus sorting source clipping points. It starts no model run, makes no source-estimator fit, and needs no GIS imports at module import time.

## Use the completed original result

From the application directory containing `model/`:

```sh
python -m model.calibration_uncertainty /path/to/original/workspace analyze EXISTING_CALIBRATION_ID --standard-errors 1
python -m model.calibration_uncertainty /path/to/original/workspace inspect RETURNED_UNCERTAINTY_ID
```

Use the actual content-addressed ID returned by the completed calibration desk. The command validates the workspace, original report, plan, observation edition and retained CSV. It then verifies that the saved candidate predictions reproduce the original objective before saving its own record.

Python API:

```python
from model.calibration_uncertainty import analyze, inspect

result = analyze(workspace, actual_calibration_id, standard_errors=1.0)
retained = inspect(workspace, result["id"])
```

The multiplier must be a finite nonnegative number. Zero gives the original point comparison; the output still reports rows lacking a published standard error. There is no arbitrary upper limit. Arithmetic that would leave the finite numerical range raises a clear error instead of creating invalid JSON or an infinite endpoint.

The application stores the result under `calibration-uncertainties/<id>.json` using the original Workspace immutable item API. Repeating the same supported analysis produces the same content-addressed result; no timestamps or random seed change that identity. The operator extension provides queue execution, linked result views and exports.

## The exact retained objective

The original calibration ranks candidates by normalized **mean squared error**. Its displayed RMSE and physical bias statistics are descriptive metrics, not the ranking objective.

Let:

- (p) identify a positive-weight pollutant.
- (w_p) be its retained objective weight and (W) the sum of those weights.
- (G_p) be the number of calibration spatial groups containing that pollutant.
- (n_{g,p}) be the number of catchment/pollutant units in a group.
- (s_p) be the retained normalization scale.
- (m_{r,i}) be the original native prediction for candidate (r) and unit (i), including the saved delivered external load.
- (y_i) be the time-weighted original annual reference for that unit.

The coefficient of each squared residual is

```text
c_i = w_p / W / G_p / n_(g,p) / s_p²
L_r(y) = sum_i c_i (m_(r,i) - y_i)²
```

Only units assigned to the original calibration groups enter this sum. The module reconstructs these coefficients and reproduces every eligible candidate's stored objective. The original scale stays fixed as source observations are perturbed. Recomputing a scale from each changed observation set would define a different objective and is outside this analysis.

All input candidate predictions must have the same complete original calibration support. Failed or ineligible native candidates retain their original report history but are not introduced into sensitivity comparisons.

## One common perturbation of original source records

A unit may combine several disjoint original annual-rate periods. For source record (j) in unit (i), the existing plan supplies period weight (t_{ij}) and aggregation weight (T_i):

```text
y_i = sum_j (t_ij / T_i) x_j
```

The module reopens the original observation rows by ID, verifies period/catchment/parameter identity and the retained uncertainty detail, and reproduces the saved mean. It uses the actual stored whole-year or elapsed-day weights. Multiple source periods do not add spatial calibration groups.

For each original source estimate (x_j) with published standard error (e_j), and selected multiplier (k), the declared marginal interval is:

```text
lower_j(k) = max(0, x_j - k e_j)
upper_j(k) = x_j + k e_j
```

A unit's interval follows from the same positive temporal weights. It is **not** presented as a newly estimated standard error of that mean. In particular, the analysis never uses a square-root-of-summed-variances formula or assumes that different years, pollutants, nested catchments or estimators are independent.

The source variable is the original observation record ID. If a record contributes to more than one unit, its coefficients are summed before evaluating bounds. Every candidate sees the same changed value of that source record. Distinct source IDs define a joint marginal box. Dependence between distinct estimates can make some combinations in this box unattainable; a strict preference throughout the whole box is therefore conservative with respect to those dependencies. A possible reversal means a reversal within the declared box, not an assigned probability or a claim about a particular unrecorded dependence model.

This analysis does not join differently named records by guessing from station names, coordinates or free-form provenance. The original observation edition and spatial grouping remain visible for source review.

## Original uncertainty semantics and units

The supported uncertainty detail is explicit:

```json
{
  "kind": "published standard error",
  "value": 1200.0,
  "unit": "kg/year",
  "original_field": "serload_a_00600"
}
```

The numbers above illustrate the field schema only. The analysis obtains values from the retained source rows and does not construct observation data from this example.

A missing value, unsupported uncertainty kind, absent source field, negative/nonfinite value, or unrecognized mass-rate unit remains visible as an uncovered source row. A standard deviation, confidence interval, percent error or opaque string is not silently reinterpreted as a standard error. The complete original uncertainty and source-record details are retained in the result.

Supported mass-rate conversions match the original observation workflow: kilograms, grams and metric tonnes per year. - All four fields are in kg/year.
- SSC `80154` and TSS `00530` preserve their original constituent identities and selected source series.
- Source standard errors belong to the selected published estimator and its original long-term reference period. They are not native model uncertainty or measurement-only uncertainty.

Original report: https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20195069  
Original metadata: https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/583f2f21e4b04fc80e3bd227

The source importer retains the exact publisher dictionary, final-method selection, load/SE field names, source period and original tokens.

## Exact pairwise bounds

Let (A) be the originally selected candidate and (B) a retained eligible challenger. The reported gap is:

```text
D_B(y) = L_B(y) - L_A(y)
```

A positive gap favors the original selection. Expanding the difference cancels the observation-squared term:

```text
D_B(y) = sum_i c_i (m_(B,i) - m_(A,i))
                         (m_(B,i) + m_(A,i) - 2 y_i)
```

For numerical evaluation the module uses a centered form:

```text
D_B(y0) = sum_i c_i (m_B - m_A) ((m_B - y0) + (m_A - y0))
q_i = -2 c_i (m_B - m_A)
Q_j = sum_i q_i t_ij / T_i
D_B(x) = D_B(x0) + sum_j Q_j (x_j - x0_j)
```

The sums use `math.fsum`. This avoids subtracting two separately accumulated large squared-loss totals.

Because the gap is affine in the common source values, the exact box extrema occur at endpoints. For the minimum, use the lower endpoint when (Q_j>0) and the upper endpoint when (Q_j<0). Reverse those choices for the maximum. A zero coefficient is invariant to that source value.

The result includes per-source coefficients, contributions to each gap extreme, and endpoint labels. These are sensitivity coordinates and contribution accounting, not replacement observations. The module does not export a constructed endpoint vector as an observation dataset.

A source with missing SE prevents a complete finite bound only when its combined coefficient is nonzero. Exact cancellation can make a pair insensitive to an uncovered record. At (k=0), the interval is the original point regardless of missing SE; published-SE coverage remains separately visible.

### Numerical tolerance

The reported tolerance is (10^{-10}) times the maximum of one and the relevant retained objective magnitudes. It is used for nominal reproduction and near-zero classification. Endpoint values and the original score gap remain visible for interpretation.

- `selected_strictly_preferred`: the minimum challenger gap is greater than tolerance.
- `rank_reversal_possible`: the minimum gap is less than negative tolerance.
- `tie_possible`: the band reaches the numerical tie region.
- `nominal_tie`: the zero-multiplier point is in the tie region.
- `equivalent_predictions`: all original calibration predictions are identical for this pair.
- `incomplete_uncertainty`: a contributing original source lacks supported SE.

The existing calibration's deterministic tie-breaking and selected ID remain unchanged. A near-zero gap does not rerank candidates.

A global `strictly_stable` result requires strict preference over every eligible challenger in the comparison cohort. Runs from the same profile but different native model selections are labeled through `same_profile_as_selected` and `selected_models`; distinct profile counts remain explicit. One available candidate produces `single_candidate`, not an unsupported dominance claim.

## First tie in published standard-error units

For each challenger the module also finds the first (kge0) at which its minimum gap reaches zero, under the same declared box and fixed objective.

For a positive source coefficient, the minimum-gap displacement is (-min(k e_j,x_j)). Its contribution becomes constant once (k=x_j/e_j), because source loads cannot fall below zero. For a negative coefficient, the minimizing displacement is (+k e_j), which has no nonnegative-load upper cap. The lower gap is therefore continuous, nonincreasing and piecewise linear.

The implementation sorts the finite positive-coefficient clipping points, computes the slope from the active source coefficients, and solves for zero in the containing segment. It recomputes active slopes with `math.fsum` after each event rather than subtracting a nearly equal saturated slope. Source SE zero contributes no slope.

`first_tie_standard_errors` contains the finite multiplier when available. `first_tie_state` gives:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `available` | A finite multiplier reaches the mathematical zero gap. |
| `nominal_tie` | The retained centered nominal gap is already zero or slightly negative within its verified numerical tolerance. |
| `never_within_nonnegative_source_box` | Clipping exhausts all relevant movement before the challenger can tie. |
| `incomplete_uncertainty` | A nonzero source coefficient has no supported published SE. |
| `beyond_finite_multiplier` | The mathematical crossing exceeds the finite numerical representation. |

The first-tie value solves the mathematical zero of the computed centered gap, while displayed preference states use the reported numerical tolerance. These are explicitly different near a numerical tie. Null values always have a reason; the JSON contains no infinity or NaN.

## Validation and coverage

Original validation groups remain held out. The supplement shows original source bands and residual ranges for the already selected candidate on validation units. It does not compare or select challengers on validation outcomes.

A saved result can have `state: partial_uncertainty` and still provide complete pairwise information for some or all candidates. The state describes published source-error coverage, including validation rows. Pairwise completeness follows actual nonzero source coefficients. The coverage table distinguishes:

- Original source rows and rows with recognized published SE.
- Calibration and validation unit counts.
- Units whose contributing source rows all have published SE.
- Missing record IDs.
- Source records used in each original partition.

A missing SE is not assigned zero. A published SE explicitly equal to zero is retained as a zero-width source band. Neither state changes the underlying original calibration result.

## Retained result and integration contract

The result has `version: 1` and Workspace schema `upstate.calibration-uncertainties/v1`.

Main objects:

- `source_stamp`: original calibration, plan and observation IDs; original retained CSV description and metadata; hashes of the frozen reference units, prediction rows, objective and normalization; original comparison IDs and source vintages.
- `candidate_scores`: every original eligible candidate's score, independently reproduced score, difference and numerical tolerance.
- `pairwise`: signed gap bounds, exact interval state, first-tie margin, native model selection, profile identity and source attribution.
- `reference_units`: original spatial/temporal identity, native units, source means/bands, original period weights and objective coefficient.
- `source_records`: source values, original units, converted SE, source uncertainty details, bands and issues.
- `selected_validation`: original selected-candidate validation residual bands.
- `coverage`, `nominal_reproduction` and `selection_sensitivity`: compact summaries for the operator view.

`inspect` validates the content-addressed supplement and its original dependency chain. It reopens the retained completed calibration, original plan and observation edition; checks frozen source/objective identities; verifies the original observation CSV byte count and SHA-256; and compares the reconstructed dependency stamp and selected IDs. This supports the existing extension verification hook and portable-workspace adoption without rerunning the analysis.

The operator adapter owns HTML, CSV and ZIP presentations. The original JSON remains the complete scientific record. Normal backups include `calibration-uncertainties` and the operator's uncertainty exports through the maintained workspace archive workflow.

## Scientific scope

The intervals describe sensitivity to the supported published source-estimate error only. They preserve the original source period and model vintage; they do not remove a mismatch between them. They also do not quantify uncertainty in native process structure, source raster inputs, reservoirs, point sources, stream-bank erosion or other omitted processes. The existing calibration result retains those interpretation inputs.

The first-tie margin and exact box comparisons provide a concrete way to identify which original source estimates matter for the current candidate decision. They help prioritize source review and additional candidate evaluation while retaining the original scientifically traceable working profile.

"""Open, render, save and independently reopen a complete package in actual QGIS.

Run with QGIS Python: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen /usr/bin/python3
    tools/model/gis_project_native.py ORIGINAL_DIRECTORY NEW_RECEIVING_DIRECTORY
The sender stays unchanged. This command carries every dataset with the project.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import sys
import time

if __package__:
    from . import gis_project as gis
else:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    import gis_project as gis


def run(directory, output):
    os.environ.setdefault("QT_QPA_PLATFORM", "offscreen")
    from qgis.core import (QgsApplication, QgsProject, QgsMapSettings,
                           QgsMapRendererParallelJob, QgsRectangle, Qgis)
    from qgis.PyQt.QtCore import QSize
    from qgis.PyQt.QtGui import QColor
    directory, output = Path(directory).resolve(strict=True), Path(output).resolve()
    before = gis.verify(directory, native=False)
    if output.exists() or output.is_relative_to(directory):
        raise FileExistsError("Choose a new receiving directory outside the sender")
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copytree(directory, output, copy_function=shutil.copyfile)
    app = QgsApplication([], False)
    app.initQgis()
    started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        project = QgsProject()
        if not project.read(str(output / "project.qgs")):
            raise ValueError("QGIS could not open the editable project")
        manifest = gis.load(output / "project.json")
        expected = {row["key"]: row for row in manifest["layers"]}
        loaded = project.mapLayers()
        if set(loaded) != set(expected):
            raise ValueError("Native QGIS layer identities differ")
        rows = []
        for key, layer in loaded.items():
            if not layer.isValid():
                raise ValueError("Native QGIS layer failed: " + layer.name())
            item = {"id": key, "name": layer.name(), "provider": layer.providerType(),
                    "crs": layer.crs().authid(), "valid": True}
            if expected[key]["data"]["kind"] == "vector":
                item["feature_count"] = layer.featureCount()
                if item["feature_count"] != expected[key]["data"]["feature_count"]:
                    raise ValueError("Native QGIS feature population differs")
            else:
                item.update(width=layer.width(), height=layer.height())
                if (item["width"], item["height"]) != (expected[key]["data"]["width"], expected[key]["data"]["height"]):
                    raise ValueError("Native QGIS raster dimensions differ")
            rows.append(item)
        settings = QgsMapSettings()
        settings.setDestinationCrs(project.crs())
        settings.setBackgroundColor(QColor("white"))
        settings.setOutputSize(QSize(1400, 950))
        settings.setLayers([node.layer() for node in project.layerTreeRoot().findLayers() if node.isVisible()])
        settings.setExtent(QgsRectangle(*manifest["extent"]))
        job = QgsMapRendererParallelJob(settings)
        job.start()
        job.waitForFinished()
        errors = [{"layer_id": item.layerID, "message": item.message} for item in job.errors()]
        if errors:
            raise ValueError("Native QGIS rendering: " + json.dumps(errors))
        if not job.renderedImage().save(str(output / "qgis-native.png")):
            raise OSError("Could not save the native rendering")
        project.setFilePathStorage(Qgis.FilePathType.Relative)
        native_file = output / "project.qgz"
        if not project.write(str(native_file)):
            raise OSError("Native QGIS save failed")
        check = QgsProject()
        if not check.read(str(native_file)) or set(check.mapLayers()) != set(expected):
            raise ValueError("The native saved project did not reopen")
        if any(not layer.isValid() for layer in check.mapLayers().values()):
            raise ValueError("A layer did not reopen from the native saved edition")
        import zipfile
        with zipfile.ZipFile(native_file) as archive:
            qgs = [n for n in archive.namelist() if n.endswith(".qgs")]
            if len(qgs) != 1:
                raise ValueError("Expected one native project XML")
            (output / "project.qgs").write_bytes(archive.read(qgs[0]))
        result = {"schema": "upstate.gis-native-receiving/v1", "version": Qgis.QGIS_VERSION,
                  "layer_count": len(rows), "layers": rows, "render_errors": errors,
                  "native_save_reopened": True, "seconds": round(time.monotonic()-started, 6)}
        gis.save(output / "native-receiving.json", result)
        manifest["native_qgis"] = {"status": "opened, rendered, saved and reopened", **result}
        gis.save(output / "project.json", manifest)
        # HTML does not depend on QGIS Python's Fiona/Rasterio installation.
        gis.catalogue(output, manifest)
        gis.inventory(output)
        gis.verify(output, native=False)
        if gis.verify(directory, native=False) != before:
            raise ValueError("Sender changed during native receiving")
        return {**result, "directory": str(output), "sender_unchanged": True}
    except Exception:
        # A failed native receive remains available for diagnosis, with no success record.
        raise
    finally:
        project = None
        app.exitQgis()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("directory")
    parser.add_argument("output")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(run(args.directory, args.output), indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Water and Habitat Context

Authored by TokenJunkieLabs.

This additive desk turns retained source editions into a saved, inspectable description of a selected reporting area. It covers mapped aquatic habitat, wetland inventory coverage, mapped hydrography, PAD-US inventory, authoritative stream order, and spatial relationships to supplied HUC or utility boundaries.

The calculation uses the existing scientific Workspace. It reads original retained vector bodies through the application's Fiona/GDAL environment and supports prepared NWI_CONTEXT rasters through their original class dictionary and mapping-status companion.

## Integration

Place these two complete files alongside the current application:

- model/water_context.py
- model/WATER_CONTEXT.md

The public interface is:

    from model import water_context
    catalog = water_context.catalog(workspace)
    record = water_context.build(workspace, spec)
    records = water_context.list_saved(workspace)
    reopened = water_context.get_saved(workspace, record["id"])
    map_data = water_context.preview(workspace, record["id"])
    verification = water_context.verify_all(workspace)

Each function accepts an existing Workspace instance or its root directory. GIS imports and original source verification occur during an explicit build. Catalog, list and get calls read retained JSON metadata. Preview reads its precomputed display artifact. The existing operator queue should invoke build; the source module creates no server, queue or model engine.

The core composes with the existing APIs:

- Workspace.sources(), _get("sources", collection_id), source_file(collection_id, source_id).
- Workspace._save("water-context-selections", spec), which returns a content-addressed immutable selection.
- model.rasters.native_vector_path and vector_environment, including original gzip carriers.
- model.common atomic_json, atomic_bytes, digest, identifier, describe_file, verify_file, relative_file and held.

## Selection specification

    {
      "title": "Upper Savannah water and habitat context",
      "boundary": {
        "collection_id": "<retained source collection hash>",
        "source_id": "<retained reporting/HUC/utility polygon source>",
        "layer": "<optional native layer>",
        "where": {"HUC12": "<optional exact native value>"},
        "id_field": "<optional native feature ID field>",
        "feature_ids": ["<optional selected native IDs>"]
      },
      "overlays": {
        "wetlands": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NWI source>"},
        "mapping_status": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NWI mapping status>"},
        "flowlines": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NHD flowline source>"},
        "waterbodies": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NHD waterbody source>"},
        "protected_lands": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<PAD-US manager inventory>"},
        "stream_order": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NHD_STREAM_ORDER source>"}
      },
      "measurement_crs": "EPSG:5070",
      "relations": [
        {"kind": "huc", "collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<HUC polygons>"},
        {"kind": "utility", "collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<utility polygons>"}
      ]
    }

All overlays and relationship sources are optional. A polygon selection is required. References accept the same layer, equality filter, native ID field and explicit ID selection as the primary boundary. NWI mapping status uses all retained status records; its where and feature_ids filters are rejected so Digital, No_Data and unknown records participate in the same partition. Select its geographic extent through the reporting boundary. Equality filters use actual native values and field names; they do not become SQL expressions. Multiple selected reporting features are dissolved for the headline denominator.

The two NHD roles remain separately selectable even when both original entries declare role NHD. The optional stream_order selector uses an independently supplied NHD_STREAM_ORDER source and its native streamorde/streamorder field. It carries native NHDPlusID and permanent_identifier values into the tables and retains all original properties. Source capture and flow routing remain with their existing components.

If wetlands selects a prepared NWI_CONTEXT raster and mapping_status is omitted, the core uses its declared mapping_status_path companion. The paired companion must be present in that exact retained source entry. The final normalized selection records this choice.
