    "operator/STATION_GEOGRAPHY.md",
    "operator/fixtures/station_geography_actual87_ids.json",
)

def sha(body):
    return hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()

def install(application, source_root, *, dry_run=False):
    application, source_root = Path(application).resolve(strict=True), Path(source_root).resolve(strict=True)
    for name in ("model/workspace.py", "model/spatial_esri.py", "operator/server.py",
                 "operator/web/app.mjs", "operator/extension_registry.py", "operator/web/extension_host.mjs"):
        if not (application / name).is_file():
            raise ValueError("Receive the complete existing application before adding station geography: " + name)
    pending, previous = {}, {}
    for name in FILES:
        body = (source_root / name).read_bytes()
        if name.endswith(".py"):
            ast.parse(body.decode("utf-8"), filename=name)
        elif name.endswith(".json"):
            value = json.loads(body)
            if name.endswith("station-geography.json") and value.get("schema") != "upstate.operator-extension/v1":
                raise ValueError("The station geography descriptor schema differs")
        pending[name] = body
        previous[name] = (application / name).read_bytes() if (application / name).exists() else None
    changed = [name for name in FILES if previous[name] != pending[name]]
    server = (application / "operator/server.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    browser = (application / "operator/web/app.mjs").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    host_needed = "ExtensionRegistry" not in server or "createExtensionHost" not in browser
    if host_needed and not (application / "install_extensions.py").is_file():
        raise ValueError("Retain the existing authored install_extensions.py to join its original operator host")
    receipt = {"schema": "upstate.station-geography-install/v1", "application": str(application),
        "dry_run": dry_run, "changed": changed, "existing_host_install_needed": host_needed,
        "files": [{"path": name, "bytes": len(pending[name]), "sha256": sha(pending[name]),
                  "previous_sha256": sha(previous[name]) if previous[name] is not None else None} for name in FILES]}
    if dry_run:
        return receipt
    stamp = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ")
    backup = application / ".station-geography-backups" / stamp
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".station-geography-install-", dir=application.parent) as temporary:
        staging = Path(temporary)
        for name in changed:
            target = staging / name
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(pending[name])
        for name in changed:
            target = application / name
            current = target.read_bytes() if target.exists() else None
            if current != previous[name]:
                raise RuntimeError("Concurrent authored source changed during station installation: " + name)
        for name in changed:
            target = application / name
            if previous[name] is not None:
                original = backup / name
                original.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                original.write_bytes(previous[name])
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            os.replace(staging / name, target)
    if host_needed:
        completed = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(application / "install_extensions.py"),
            "--application", str(application), "--source-root", str(application)],
            check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=application)
        receipt["original_host_install"] = json.loads(completed.stdout)
    receipt["installed_at"] = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat()
    receipt_path = application / "operator" / "station-geography-install.json"
    receipt_path.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return receipt

def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--application", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--source-root", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    print(json.dumps(install(args.application, args.source_root, dry_run=args.dry_run), indent=2, sort_keys=True))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Copyright TokenJunkieLabs. Retain the application license and source notices.
"""Own the original operator and receiving-water browser in one native invocation."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import signal
import sys

APP = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(APP))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from receiving import OperatorProcess, atomic, record, run_command
from model.common import digest, held, identifier, now, read_json
from model.workspace import Workspace
from model import receiving_waters

SCHEMA = "upstate.receiving-water-browser-owner/v1"


def existing_executable(value, title):
    candidate = shutil.which(value) if value else None
    if candidate is None and value:
        candidate = str(Path(value).expanduser().resolve())
    if not candidate or not Path(candidate).is_file() or not os.access(candidate, os.X_OK):
        raise ValueError("Select the installed " + title + " executable")
    return str(Path(candidate).resolve())


def original_preparation(path):
    path = path.expanduser().resolve(strict=True)
    value = read_json(path)
    if value.get("schema") != "upstate.public-water-preparation/v1":
        raise ValueError("Select the original public-water preparation result")
    if value.get("plan_state") != "complete":
        raise ValueError("The original source preparation has not completed its plan")
    root = Path(value["workspace"])
    if not root.is_absolute():
        raise ValueError("Preparation must retain its absolute original Workspace")
    workspace = Workspace(root.resolve(strict=True))
    plan = receiving_waters.inspect_plan(workspace, identifier(value["plan_id"]))
    if plan["state"] != "complete":
        raise ValueError("The original saved source plan is incomplete")
    if set(value["receptor_ids"]) != {row["id"] for row in plan["receptors"]}:
        raise ValueError("Preparation receptor IDs differ from the original saved plan")
    if any(row["source"]["source_collection_id"] != value["source_collection_id"]
           for row in plan["receptors"]):
        raise ValueError("Preparation source collection differs from the original saved plan")
    return workspace, plan, record(path)


def operate(args):
    workspace, plan, preparation = original_preparation(args.preparation)
    if args.analysis_id:
        analysis = receiving_waters.inspect(workspace, identifier(args.analysis_id))
        if analysis["state"] != "complete" or analysis["plan_id"] != plan["id"]:
            raise ValueError("Select a completed analysis of the original prepared plan")
    node = existing_executable(args.node, "Node")
    chromium = existing_executable(args.chromium, "Chromium") if args.chromium else None
    modules = args.node_modules
    if modules:
        modules = str(Path(modules).expanduser().resolve(strict=True))
        if not (Path(modules) / "playwright" / "index.mjs").is_file():
            raise ValueError("The selected node_modules directory does not contain installed Playwright")
    root = args.output_dir.expanduser().resolve()
    if root.is_relative_to(workspace.root):
        raise ValueError("Choose browser receiving output outside the scientific Workspace")
    state = (args.operator_state.expanduser().resolve() if args.operator_state
             else workspace.root.with_name(workspace.root.name + "-operator"))
    if state.is_relative_to(workspace.root):
        raise ValueError("Keep original operator state outside the scientific Workspace")
    source_paths = (
        "operator/receiving_water_operate.py", "operator/receiving.py",
        "operator/receiving_water_browser.mjs", "operator/server.py",
        "operator/web/app.mjs", "operator/web/receiving_waters.mjs",
        "operator/web/receiving_water_spatial.mjs", "operator/web/spatial.mjs",
        "model/receiving_water_spatial.py", "model/spatial.py",
        "model/spatial_exports.py", "model/cartography.py", "model/rasters.py",
    )
    sources = [{"name": name, **record(APP / name)} for name in source_paths]
    identity = {
        "schema": SCHEMA, "project_id": workspace.project["id"],
        "workspace": str(workspace.root), "plan_id": plan["id"],
        "analysis_id": args.analysis_id,
        "preparation": preparation, "operator_state": str(state),
        "application_identity": digest([
            {key: row[key] for key in ("name", "bytes", "sha256")} for row in sources
        ]),
        "runtime": {"python": sys.executable, "node": node,
                    "node_modules": modules, "chromium": chromium},
        "selection": {"paper": args.paper, "dpi": args.dpi,
                      "task_timeout_seconds": args.task_timeout_seconds},
    }
    operation_id = digest(identity)
    directory = root / operation_id
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
    os.chmod(directory, 0o700)
    result_path = directory / "receiving-water-owner.json"
    ready_path = directory / "operator-ready.private.json"
    control_path = directory / "browser-control.private.json"
    result = {**identity, "id": operation_id, "state": "running",
              "started_at": now(), "application_root": str(APP),
              "application_files": sources, "result_path": str(result_path),
              "operator_started": False, "operator_closed": False}

    def publish(stage):
        result.update(stage=stage, updated_at=now())
        atomic(result_path, result)
        print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "operation_id": operation_id,
                          "result_path": str(result_path)}), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)

    with held(directory / ".receiving-water-browser.lock", blocking=False):
        server = None
        try:
            publish("start_original_operator")
            server = OperatorProcess(APP, workspace.root, state, directory / "received",
                                     directory, "receiving-water", 4096)
            if server.receipt["project"]["id"] != workspace.project["id"]:
                raise ValueError("Original operator opened a different scientific Workspace")
            result["operator_started"] = True
            result["workspace_key"] = server.receipt["workspace_key"]
            result["operator_process_id"] = server.child.pid
            atomic(ready_path, server.receipt)
            control = {
                "ready_file": str(ready_path),
                "output": str(directory / "browser"),
                "workspace_key": server.receipt["workspace_key"],
                "plan_id": plan["id"], "paper": args.paper, "dpi": args.dpi,
                "task_timeout_seconds": args.task_timeout_seconds,
            }
            for key, value in (("analysis_id", args.analysis_id),
                               ("node_modules", modules), ("chromium", chromium)):
                if value is not None:
                    control[key] = value
            atomic(control_path, control)
            publish("operate_original_browser")
            run_command([node, str(APP / "operator/receiving_water_browser.mjs"),
                         str(control_path)], directory, "receiving-water-browser")
            browser_path = directory / "browser" / "receiving-water-browser.json"
            browser = read_json(browser_path)
            if not browser.get("complete") or browser.get("project_id") != workspace.project["id"]:
                raise ValueError("The original browser did not complete this Workspace")
            if browser.get("plan_id") != plan["id"] or browser.get("analysis_id") != args.analysis_id:
                raise ValueError("The completed browser selected a different plan or analysis")
            if not browser.get("cases") or any(
                not row.get("saved_and_exported") or not row.get("cold_reopened")
                for row in browser["cases"].values()
            ):
                raise ValueError("The original browser has unfinished saved/exported/reopened maps")
            result.update(browser_result=record(browser_path),
                          exported_maps=len(browser["cases"]),
                          browser_application_identity=browser["application_identity"])
            publish("drain_original_operator")
        except BaseException as error:
            result.update(state="failed", failed_at=now(),
                          error={"type": type(error).__name__, "message": str(error)})
        finally:
            if server is not None:
                try:
                    server.close()
                    result.update(operator_closed=server.child.poll() is not None,
                                  operator_exit_code=server.child.returncode)
                    if server.child.returncode != 0:
                        result.update(state="failed", failed_at=now(),
                                      closure_error={"type": "OperatorExit",
                                                     "message": "Owned operator exited " + str(server.child.returncode)})
                except BaseException as error:
                    result.update(state="failed", failed_at=now(),
                                  closure_error={"type": type(error).__name__, "message": str(error)})
            ready_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            control_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            if result["state"] == "running":
                result.update(state="complete", stage="complete", completed_at=now())
            atomic(result_path, result)
    return result


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--preparation", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--node", default=os.environ.get("CODEX_PRIMARY_RUNTIME_NODE", "node"))
    parser.add_argument("--node-modules", default=os.environ.get("CODEX_PRIMARY_RUNTIME_NODE_MODULES"))
    parser.add_argument("--chromium")
    parser.add_argument("--operator-state", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--analysis-id")
    parser.add_argument("--paper", choices=("letter", "a4"), default="letter")
    parser.add_argument("--dpi", type=int, choices=(150, 220, 300), default=220)
    parser.add_argument("--task-timeout-seconds", type=int, default=1800)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.task_timeout_seconds <= 0:
        parser.error("Select a positive duration for observing each original task")
    def stop(signum, _frame):
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_DFL)
        raise KeyboardInterrupt("Receiving-water owner interrupted by signal " + str(signum))

    previous_term = signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
    try:
        try:
            result = operate(args)
        except BaseException as error:
            result = {"schema": SCHEMA, "state": "failed", "stage": "open_original_operation",
                      "error": {"type": type(error).__name__, "message": str(error)}}
    finally:
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, previous_term)
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False, indent=2))
    return 0 if result["state"] == "complete" else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Regional soil operator desk

**Needs expert review — scientific source interpretation and spatial coverage.**

This installed operator extension connects the maintained regional USDA capture,
native K preparation and HUC12 coverage modules to the existing task queue,
source browser, source object bank and Workspace import/export flow.

## Open and use the desk

Start the existing operator with its normal workspace and registered source
roots. The shared extension registry discovers
`operator/extensions/regional-soil.json` and adds **Regional soil** beside
**Prepare study inputs**. Its source browser reads the same authorized host
roots and imported source collections as the existing preparation desk.

Three operations form the workflow:

1. **Capture the original regional soil.** Select the retained 217-HUC
   `sources.json` with its original companions, or upload the complete original
   domain ZIP. The source identity is checked against
   `upstate-wbd-upstream-domain-20261012` and its retained native geometry SHA256.
   This operation uses the original USDA interpretation metadata already in
   the application. It runs before NLCD preparation.
2. **Continue or adopt the existing soil capture.** Browse to the original
   native capture's `plan.json`. The existing plan supplies its vintage,
   projected CRS, tile size, halo, request page size and rating batch size.
   The task writes to that same capture directory and reuses its retained
   request bodies. For the active GIS12/2799 operation, select that existing
   plan rather than starting another acquisition.
3. **Prepare K and regional coverage.** Choose a completed capture in this
   study, an imported `SOIL_K_NATIVE` source, or the existing native plan.
   Select the original numeric 30 m NLCD reference. An optional original
   reporting polygon allows separate reporting-area coverage. The operation
   prepares K, computes coverage and imports both scientific sources.

The normal task history exposes queued, running, failed, interrupted and
completed work. **Resume** uses the same task identity. Actual USDA progress
reports retained tiles, mapunits received and mapunits rated. No completion
percentage is estimated while the native source has no measured total.

## Scientific selections

The existing regional source selection uses EPSG:5070 capture geometry with
a 1,000 m buffer around the original upstream domain, 15 km capture tiles,
60 m request halo, 128 native geometries per page and 1,000 mapunits per
rating batch. The original domain has 217 HUC12 units; 116 intersect the
reporting area and 101 are additional upstream units. These reporting flags
remain original attributes; an actual reporting polygon is needed for
reporting-area pixel totals.

The regional capture retrieves native whole-soil K using
`chorizon.kwfact`, Dominant Condition / Surface Layer. Original nulls remain
explicit. Preparation applies the customary-to-SI factor 0.1317 once, uses
the actual reference grid and requires 30 m north-up projected cells.

The selectable `nlcd-water-zero` policy gives zero only to unresolved,
non-conflicting pixels identified by numeric NLCD code 11. Unresolved land
and conflicting soil geometry remain NoData. The `preserve` policy retains
all unresolved values. Coverage measures valid K, unresolved land, water,
reference gaps and grid omissions separately.

The coverage result displays the 217-unit counts and unresolved-land/grid
omission counts, and provides the complete JSON summary and per-HUC12 CSV
as ordinary task downloads. Buffered model-domain, original HUC12-union and
selected reporting-area summaries remain distinct. Source maps and the
coverage status raster stay in the imported edition.

The extension uses the current SourcePreparation object's retained source

Completed capture banks travel with the Workspace. A receiving operator can

Native capture locations are indexed by original domain bytes, original

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Materialize a published-study source bank from its raw JSON or Slack Canvas Markdown."""
import argparse
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import re
import tempfile


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("bank")
    parser.add_argument("destination")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    raw = Path(args.bank).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").replace("\u00a0", " ")
    try:
        bank = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        blocks = re.findall(r"(?ms)^\x60{3}json[ \t]*\n(.*?)^\x60{3}", raw)
        banks = [json.loads(block) for block in blocks]
        bank = next(item for item in banks if item.get("schema") == "commons.source-bank/v1")
    if bank.get("schema") != "commons.source-bank/v1":
        raise SystemExit("Expected commons.source-bank/v1.")
    root = Path(args.destination).resolve()
    files, paths = [], set()
    for entry in bank["files"]:
        relative = entry["path"]
        path = PurePosixPath(relative)
        if not relative or "\\" in relative or "\x00" in relative or path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts or str(path) != relative:
            raise SystemExit("Unsafe source path: " + relative)
        if relative in paths:
            raise SystemExit("Duplicate source path: " + relative)
        paths.add(relative)
        data = base64.b64decode(entry["content_base64"], validate=True)
        if len(data) != entry["bytes"] or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != entry["sha256"]:
            raise SystemExit("Source checksum mismatch: " + relative)
        target = (root / relative).resolve()
        if not target.is_relative_to(root):
            raise SystemExit("Source path leaves destination: " + relative)
        files.append((relative, target, data))
    for relative, target, data in files:
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if target.is_file() and target.read_bytes() == data:
            continue
        fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="." + target.name + "-", dir=target.parent)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as output:
                output.write(data)
            os.replace(temporary, target)
        finally:
            if os.path.exists(temporary):
                os.unlink(temporary)
    print(json.dumps({
        "operation_id": bank.get("operation_id"), "destination": str(root),
        "files": len(files), "source_bytes": sum(len(data) for _, _, data in files),
    }, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Saved conservation plans → editable native scenarios

This is the current **Upstate** saved-plan adapter. It is separate from the earlier `eco_bridge.py` field-factor adapter. The original conservation module selects and records plans; this workbench edits geometry after receiving those original records. The original `Workspace` remains the only scientific importer, scenario writer and run preparer.

## Browser workflow

Start the normal editor, then choose **Import saved plan**. Select the complete `upstate.conservation-binding/v1` JSON produced by the original `model.conservation_bindings.bind_plan(workspace, plan_id, include_geometry=True)` operation. Choose the exact original geometry view: reporting portions by unit, whole selected units, reporting union, or whole-unit union. No alternative view is inferred.

The complete original binding bytes—including Unicode, JSON numeric representation and an optional UTF-8 BOM—are retained inside the immutable project baseline. Original selected string identifiers, including leading zeros, source-edition keys, native run/source descriptors, plan/study references, scientific contract and projected-plane hectares remain present. The original selected units are not reranked. Display geometry is the original consumer's WGS84 view; its source descriptors continue to identify the original native-CRS files and companions.

Create an alternative, edit its polygons, optionally draw new ones, exclude fields or add notes, and save. **All included polygons in the selected alternative** become the treatment footprint. The map's geodesic measurements describe edited display geometry; they do not replace the saved plan's projected-area fields. Edits can extend beyond the original selection: the exported original reference explains provenance, not a claim that the new geometry is identical to that selection.

Choose **Land-cover scenario** and enter explicit source and destination land-cover codes and a reason. The original model checks these against its retained raster and biophysical-table selection. Optionally provide actual saved grid/profile IDs and the original selected model names to prepare a native run. Numeric property edits are handled by the separate field-factor adapter and cannot silently enter this geometry/code path.

**Export complete native handover** writes:

- `design.geojson` and the unchanged parsed original `baseline.geojson`;
- exact `conservation-binding.json`, a complete independently editable `design-project.zip`, and `native-selection.json`;
- the per-file inventory and receiving guide.

The nested editable project reopens through **Receive project**, including its original binding, alternatives, notes and source properties. An independently received project gets a new editor ID; its sender is unchanged. Native model input objects remain in the original Workspace or its complete portable restoration, referenced by the original consumer. The design ZIP is not a replacement for that scientific Workspace archive.

# ECO Scenario Design

An offline field-geometry and explicit-input authoring workbench. It complements the maintained ECO Python Workspace, scenario compiler and experiment/results consoles: design original field inputs here, then use the original ECO pipeline to evaluate them.

## Start

Python 3.10+ with Shapely 2.x and pyproj 3.5+ is required. The browser has no network dependencies, map tiles, telemetry, API keys, build step or package manager.

```sh
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python server.py --workspace ./saved-designs --port 8848
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8848` in a browser on that machine. The service binds loopback. Keep the original model server on its existing port; this additive editor is independent of its renderer and routes. Use `python` rather than `python3` on Windows, and activate `.venv\Scripts\activate` there.

## Complete operator workflow

1. **Import fields** loads the original WGS84 GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Use the maintained native workspace's exact field dataset when preparing native registration. Original features, identifiers, unrelated properties, multipart polygons, holes and Z coordinates remain in the saved baseline.
2. **New** creates an independently editable alternative. Give it a name and design intent. The baseline itself is not editable.
3. Select a field. **Bind** turns a chosen numeric source property into an explicit control with a label, units and optional limits. Changes do not run a response formula. Add a field note and inspect the complete before/after ledger.
4. **Edit vertices** exposes vertices for every polygon part and hole. Drag to move, double-click an edge to insert, or select a vertex and press Delete. **Edit coordinates** supports complete Polygon/MultiPolygon JSON. Invalid rings, self-intersections and implausible longitude wrapping are rejected before saving.
5. **Draw polygon** creates an additional field with a unique identifier. Its name and identifier are editable in the inspector. Excluding a field changes only that alternative. Use duplicate, undo/redo, baseline outline and fit/zoom/pan as needed.
6. **Save** persists a revision. Autosave also runs after editing pauses. **Projects** reopens saved work; **Revisions** receives an earlier revision as a separate editable project. Browser recovery and **Local copy** retain unsaved work across interrupted sessions.
7. **Export handover** sends the complete project, original parsed GeoJSON, every realized alternative, full action ledger, standalone HTML summary and checksums. **Receive project** verifies the ZIP and creates a new project identity; subsequent receiving-side edits leave the sender unchanged. The JSON local copy is also receivable.
8. **ECO scenario** exports a native plan. Confirm every original-property-to-native-factor mapping. Choose original `field_id` or GeoJSON `id` selectors. Geometry changes select a separately received input edition. Use the native bridge below to complete registration or receiving.

## Current Upstate conservation scenarios

Choose **Import saved plan** to receive the original complete conservation binding, edit an independent geometry alternative, and export a complete **Land-cover scenario** handover. `conservation.py` uses the current original `Workspace.import_sources`, `save_scenario` and `prepare_run` interfaces, preserving selected native IDs, source editions, projected-area context and original binding bytes. See [CONSERVATION.md](CONSERVATION.md) for browser/CLI operation and exact native receiving.

## Earlier v5 field-factor bridge

The interface is the maintained v5 `model.scenarios.scenario_from_dict` → `Workspace.put_scenario` contract documented in the private ECO source canvas `F0C8F3MKR3M`. Native actions have this shape:

```json
{
  "kind": "set_factor",
  "layer": "fields",
  "selector": {"field_id": ["A1"]},
  "params": {"factor": "forest_density_multiplier", "value": 0.9}
}
```

The bridge preserves original identifier types and checks uniqueness across the effective field population. It will not silently omit an edited control that lacks a mapping. Create a mapping file, for example `factor-map.json`:

```json
{"forest_density_multiplier": "forest_density_multiplier"}
```

The names must come from the actual maintained model configuration. The example is the published v5 forest-density factor; other source properties need their own correct factor names. Alternative IDs are in `project.json`, not their editable display names.

Create a complete native plan without writing a native workspace:

```sh
python eco_bridge.py editable-project.json \
  --alternative alt_YOUR_ID --factor-map factor-map.json \
  --output native-plan.json
```

Register a factor-only alternative through the original maintained writer:

```sh

  --eco-source /path/to/ecodss/python/source \
  --native-workspace /path/to/saved/native/workspace --register
```

Use the exported ZIP in place of `editable-project.json` for direct verified receiving. The source field dataset must match the imported baseline. Scenario IDs are content-derived and repeat registration is idempotent; conflicting existing IDs are never overwritten. This operation adds a scenario to the selected workspace through its original writer. Do not run a concurrent native manifest edit during this file-writer operation.

For reshaped, added or excluded fields, receive a separate complete native input edition:

```sh

  --materialized-inputs \
  --eco-source /path/to/ecodss/python/source \
  --native-workspace /path/to/saved/native/workspace \
  --receive-workspace /path/to/new/geometry-edition
```

Every original workspace file is copied. The new edition retains the original workspace manifest, original field bytes and full editable design under `design-handover/`. Its field dataset expresses the geometry/inclusion changes; numeric changes remain native `set_factor` actions. A derived dataset ID and source provenance distinguish this changed input population. Only its intended new scenario is registered, rather than relabeling original scenarios over changed geometry. Original model and uncertainty parameters are preserved. New destination creation is exclusive and existing destinations are refused. Datasets must reside inside the original workspace and symlinks must be resolved to ordinary portable files first.

The receiving bridge does not start model runs. Open the received edition in the maintained ECO Workspace and evaluate it with the same original experiment runner used by the rest of the product. Pairing/independent-evaluation rules and calibrated data remain the responsibility of that original evaluation workflow.

## Storage and portability

`--workspace` contains `projects.sqlite3`, using SQLite WAL and transactionally retained revisions. Each save supplies an expected revision. A stale browser gets an explicit conflict rather than overwriting newer work. Original baseline changes are refused for existing projects. To back up a live store, use SQLite's backup API or stop the editor and copy its workspace; do not copy only the main database while WAL writes are active.

Export without starting HTTP:

```sh
python server.py --workspace ./saved-designs \
  --export PROJECT_UUID --output editable-handover.zip
```

`baseline.geojson` preserves the parsed original collection, not its input whitespace. Original input byte hashes identify source text when available. Integral floating-point JSON values are canonicalized consistently with browser JSON serialization before hashing, so `1.0` and `1` cannot create a false immutable-baseline conflict.

## Geometry and operating range

Input is WGS84/CRS84 longitude/latitude Polygon or MultiPolygon GeoJSON. There is no automatic CRS guessing or reprojection. Areas are ellipsoidal geodesic measurements from pyproj; displayed totals sum field areas and include overlap. This is a regional planar editing view with geodesic measurement, not a global/antimeridian editor. Imported collections must span less than 180 degrees longitude. The engine admits up to 25,000 features, 1,000,000 vertices, 100 alternatives and 250 parameter bindings; these are validation ceilings, not measured interactive performance guarantees. Requests and project ZIPs have explicit size limits. Search narrows the field list; the first 500 matching field labels are rendered.

"""Build the complete deterministic source ZIP and per-file content inventory."""
import argparse,hashlib,json,zipfile
from pathlib import Path

def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);ap.add_argument('output',type=Path);args=ap.parse_args()
    root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    if args.output.resolve().is_relative_to(root):ap.error('Place the archive outside the source root')
    files=sorted(p for p in root.rglob('*') if p.is_file() and '__pycache__' not in p.parts and p.name!='SOURCE_MANIFEST.json' and p.suffix!='.pyc')
    manifest={str(p.relative_to(root)):{'bytes':p.stat().st_size,'sha256':hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()} for p in files}
    (root/'SOURCE_MANIFEST.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest,indent=2)+'\n');files.append(root/'SOURCE_MANIFEST.json')
    with zipfile.ZipFile(args.output,'w',compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,compresslevel=9) as z:
        for p in sorted(files):
            info=zipfile.ZipInfo('scenario-design/'+str(p.relative_to(root)),date_time=(2026,10,12,0,0,0))

# Additional WQP locations for the 159-station assessment study

The original published 2024 and July 2026 assessment banks select 192 cause records at 159 distinct stations in the exact retained 217-HUC domain. Original SCDES Atlas STAT matching locates 152 stations; the existing eight-station WQP source locates five more. This separate source supplies RS-21038 and RS-22075 from their official WQP station pages.

## Import and select

Import `sources.json` through the existing Workspace source importer. Select source ID `scdes-wqp-assessment159-additional-two-20261013` as an additional monitoring-station source with `station_id_field=MonitoringLocationName`, `id_field=MonitoringLocationIdentifier` and `source_crs=EPSG:4326`. Keep the existing 705-feature Atlas and WQP8 source references beside it.

The two point coordinates copy the original longitude/latitude strings reported on the official pages. Both source pages explicitly report WGS84. The GeoJSON preserves every metadata value shown in each page table as a string; the retained extraction companion preserves the retrieved page text and exact primary URLs. The source representation is a derivation from official station-page metadata.

`assessment159_native_identity_crosswalk.csv` records all 159 station/source/native-ID matches in each source's native CRS. Its station publisher HUCs and assessment HUCs stay separate. Original assessment record IDs remain edition-specific. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Install the cumulative Upper Savannah source in a fresh application directory.

Uses the retained component authors' source transformations, composes their shared
lifecycle hooks, restores bundled original input bytes, and publishes one complete
application ZIP. Run with the existing scientific Python environment.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import runpy
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import traceback
import zipfile

OPERATION = "UPSTATE-INTEGRATED-DELIVERY-ECD1-20261012"
RECORD = "CUMULATIVE_INSTALLATION.json"
SHARED = ("operator/server.py", "operator/web/app.mjs",
          "operator/web/index.html", "model/portable.py")


def sha(body):
    return hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()


def replace(text, before, after, label):
    if after in text and (before in after or before not in text):
        return text
    if not before or text.count(before) != 1:
        raise ValueError(label + ": expected one current source anchor")
    return text.replace(before, after, 1)


def owned_inventory(root):
    entries = {}
    for path in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
        relative = path.relative_to(root)
        if any(p in {"__pycache__", ".git", ".venv", "venv", "node_modules"} for p in relative.parts):
            continue
        if any(p.startswith(".") for p in relative.parts) or path.suffix in {".pyc", ".pyo", ".lock"}:
            continue
        if relative.as_posix() in {"APPLICATION_SOURCE_RECEIPT.json", RECORD}:
            continue
        if path.is_symlink():
            raise ValueError("Application source contains a file alias: " + str(relative))
        if path.is_file():
            digest = hashlib.sha256()
            size = 0
            with path.open("rb") as stream:
                first = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
                for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                    digest.update(block)
                    size += len(block)
                last = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
            fields = ("st_dev", "st_ino", "st_size", "st_mtime_ns", "st_ctime_ns")
            if (any(getattr(first, field) != getattr(last, field) for field in fields)
                    or size != first.st_size):
                raise ValueError("Application source changed while being inventoried: " + str(relative))
            entries[relative.as_posix()] = {
                "bytes": size, "sha256": digest.hexdigest(),
                "mode": "100755" if first.st_mode & 0o111 else "100644",
            }
    return entries


def identity(entries):
    return sha((json.dumps(entries, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n").encode())


def write(path, body):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else body)


def module(root, name):
    return runpy.run_path(str(root / name), run_name="_cumulative_" + name.replace("/", "_").replace(".", "_"))


def apply_function(root, transforms, label, records):
    changes = []
    pending = {}
    for relative, function in transforms:
        original = (root / relative).read_text("utf-8")
        result = function(original)
        if relative.endswith(".py"):
            ast.parse(result, filename=relative)
        if result != original:
            pending[relative] = result
            changes.append({"path": relative, "before": sha(original.encode()),
                            "after": sha(result.encode())})
    for relative, result in pending.items():
        write(root / relative, result)
    records.append({"component": label, "changes": changes})


def diagnostic_join(root, records):
    package = module(root, "operator/install_diagnostics.py")
    pending, changes = {}, []
    for item in package["PATCHES"]:
        path = item["path"]
        text = pending.setdefault(path, (root / path).read_text("utf-8"))
        before, after = item["anchor"], item["replacement"]
        if item["key"] == "app-workspace-detach":
            # Earlier scenario-analysis registration owns its own detach call.
            # Insert this controller at the original workspace assignment.
            before, after = "workspace=id;", "experimentDiagnostics.detach();workspace=id;"
        result = replace(text, before, after, "Scientific interpretation " + item["key"])
        pending[path] = result
        if result != text:
            changes.append(item["key"])
    for path, text in pending.items():
        if path.endswith(".py"):
            ast.parse(text, filename=path)
    for path, text in pending.items():
        write(root / path, text)
    records.append({"component": "Scientific interpretation", "joins": changes})


def restore_inputs(root):
    path = root / "integration/source_binary_inputs.json"
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    bank = json.loads(path.read_text("utf-8"))
    if bank.get("schema") != "commons.embedded-source-inputs/v1":
        raise ValueError("Choose the complete retained source input bank")
    from source_tools.application_assembly import member_name
    restored = []
    for item in bank["files"]:
        name = member_name(item["path"])
        data = base64.b64decode(item["content_base64"], validate=True)
        if len(data) != item["bytes"] or sha(data) != item["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Retained input identity differs: " + str(name))
        target = root.joinpath(*name.parts)
        if target.exists() and target.read_bytes() != data:
            raise ValueError("Another original input owns " + str(name))
        write(target, data)
        restored.append({"path": str(name), "bytes": len(data), "sha256": sha(data)})
    return restored


def shared_lifecycle(root):
    path = root / "operator/web/app.mjs"
    text = path.read_text("utf-8")
    controllers = [
        ("experiments", "experiments"), ("conservation", "conservation"),
        ("experimentDiagnostics", "experiment-diagnostics"),
        ("chemistry", "chemistry"), ("programmes", "programmes"),
    ]
    installed = [(name, view) for name, view in controllers
                 if ("const " + name + "=") in text or ("const " + name + " =") in text]
    lines = ["  // Cumulative lifecycle: detach only desks outside the selected view."]
    lines += ["  if(view!==" + json.dumps(view) + ")" + name + ".detach();"
              for name, view in installed]
    if "const extensions=" in text or "const extensions =" in text:
        lines.append("  if(!extensions.hasView(view))extensions.detach();")
    addition = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    anchor = "function render(){\n  if(!state)return;\n"
    text = replace(text, anchor, anchor + addition, "complete desk view lifecycle")
    guard = " if(formDialog.open)throw Error('Finish or close the current draft before changing workspaces.');\n"
    cleanup = "".join(" " + name + ".detach();\n" for name, _ in installed)
    text = text.replace("async function selectWorkspace(id){\n conservation.detach();\n",
                        "async function selectWorkspace(id){\n", 1)
    text = replace(text, guard, guard + cleanup, "desk lifecycle after original draft guard")
    # The shared-host installer has emitted both authored fallback spellings.
    # Normalize the older fallback before accepting the current one on replay.
    old_confirmation = "toast((actionLabels[action]||action)+' retained.');"
    confirmation = "toast((actionLabels[action] || action)+' retained.');"
    if old_confirmation in text:
        text = replace(text, old_confirmation, confirmation,
                       "registered action completion label")
    else:
        text = replace(text, "toast(actionLabels[action]+' retained.');",
                       confirmation, "registered action completion label")
    write(path, text)

    index = root / "operator/web/index.html"
    html = index.read_text("utf-8")
    if any(view == "chemistry" for _, view in installed) and 'data-view="chemistry"' not in html:
        anchor = '    <button data-view="observations">'
        html = replace(html, anchor,
                       '    <button data-view="chemistry">Reach chemistry</button>\n' + anchor,
                       "Reach chemistry navigation")
    write(index, html)


def compose(root, records=None):
    if records is None:
        records = []
    diagnostic_join(root, records)
    experiments = module(root, "install_experiments.py")
    apply_function(root, [
        ("operator/server.py", experiments["server_join"]),

    """Join complete original study and geography sources to the maintained host."""
    def complete(label, paths):
        present = [(root / name).is_file() for name in paths]
        if not any(present):
            return False
        missing = [name for name, exists in zip(paths, present) if not exists]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(label + " source cohort is incomplete: " + ", ".join(missing))
        return True

    def manifest(relative):
        path = root / relative
        document = json.loads(path.read_text("utf-8-sig"))
        if document.get("schema") != "upstate.sources/v1" or not document.get("entries"):
            raise ValueError("Receive the populated original source manifest: " + relative)
        members = {}
        for entry in document["entries"]:
            for item in (entry, *entry.get("companions", [])):
                name = item.get("path")
                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or "\\" in name or "\0" in name:
                    raise ValueError("The original manifest has an invalid member: " + relative)
                original = path.parent / name
                resolved = original.resolve(strict=True)
                if not resolved.is_relative_to(root.resolve()):
                    raise ValueError("Source member leaves the complete application: " + relative)
                current = root
                for part in original.relative_to(root).parts:
                    current = current / part
                    if current.is_symlink():
                        raise ValueError("Source member uses a filesystem alias: " + str(original))
                if not resolved.is_file():
                    raise ValueError("Source member is not an ordinary file: " + str(original))
                body = resolved.read_bytes()
                if item.get("bytes") is not None and len(body) != item["bytes"]:
                    raise ValueError("Original source member length differs: " + str(original))
                if item.get("sha256") is not None and sha(body) != item["sha256"]:
                    raise ValueError("Original source member hash differs: " + str(original))
                key = resolved.relative_to(root.resolve()).as_posix()
                members[key] = {"path": key, "bytes": len(body), "sha256": sha(body)}
        return {"path": relative, "sha256": sha(path.read_bytes()),
