def guided_join(root, records):
    """Compose the author's full verified component in this fresh staging tree."""
    path = root / "operator/install_guided_journey.py"
    if not path.is_file():
        return
    package = module(root, "operator/install_guided_journey.py")
    manifest, files, integration = package["read_component"](root)
    original, proposed, modes = package["prepare"](root, files, integration)
    changes = []
    for name, body in proposed.items():
        if name.endswith(".py"):
            ast.parse(body.decode("utf-8"), filename=name)
        if name.endswith(".json"):
            json.loads(body)
        if original[name] != body:
            changes.append({"path": name,
                            "before": sha(original[name]) if original[name] is not None else None,
                            "after": sha(body)})
    for name, body in proposed.items():
        if original[name] != body:
            target = root / name
            write(target, body)
            target.chmod(modes[name])
    records.append({"component": "Guided journey",
                    "operation_id": manifest["operation_id"], "changes": changes})


def check_sources(root):
    python = 0
    for path in sorted(root.rglob("*.py")):
        if "__pycache__" in path.parts:
            continue
        ast.parse(path.read_text("utf-8"), filename=str(path.relative_to(root)))
        python += 1
    node = shutil.which("node")
    javascript = "browser receiving"
    if node:
        result = subprocess.run([node, "--check", str(root / "operator/web/app.mjs")],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45)
        if result.returncode:
            raise ValueError(result.stderr.strip() or "Combined browser module did not parse")
        javascript = "combined operator module parsed"
    return {"python_modules": python, "javascript": javascript}


def archive_record(path):
    """Describe a completed ZIP without loading the compressed payload in RAM."""
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    size = 0
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        before = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
            size += len(block)
        after = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
    identity = lambda info: (info.st_dev, info.st_ino, info.st_size,
                             info.st_mtime_ns, info.st_ctime_ns)
    if identity(before) != identity(after) or size != before.st_size:
        raise ValueError("Application archive changed while its identity was recorded")
    return {"path": str(path), "bytes": size, "sha256": digest.hexdigest()}


def same_archive_members(current, proposed):
    """Compare original uncompressed members with bounded working memory."""
    names = current.namelist()
    if names != proposed.namelist():
        return False
    for name in names:
        if current.getinfo(name).file_size != proposed.getinfo(name).file_size:
            return False
        with current.open(name) as left, proposed.open(name) as right:
            while True:
                first, second = left.read(1024 * 1024), right.read(1024 * 1024)
                if first != second:
                    return False
                if not first:
                    break
    return True


def archive_application(root, destination):
    destination = Path(destination).absolute()
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = None
    try:
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(prefix=".application-", dir=destination.parent, delete=False) as stream:
            temporary = Path(stream.name)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(temporary, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,
                             compresslevel=6, strict_timestamps=False) as archive:
            for path in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
                if path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not any(
                        part.startswith(".") or part == "__pycache__"
                        for part in path.relative_to(root).parts):
                    archive.write(path, "upper-savannah-application/" + path.relative_to(root).as_posix())
        if destination.exists():
            # Compressed transport can differ across zlib versions. Existing
            # output is compared by its complete retained uncompressed members.
            with zipfile.ZipFile(destination) as current, zipfile.ZipFile(temporary) as proposed:
                if not same_archive_members(current, proposed):
                    raise ValueError("Another complete application owns " + str(destination))
            return archive_record(destination)
        record = archive_record(temporary)
        with temporary.open("rb") as stream:
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.link(temporary, destination)
        return {**record, "path": str(destination)}
    finally:
        if temporary:
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def install(source, output, archive):
    source, output = Path(source).resolve(strict=True), Path(output).absolute()
    if not (source / "model/workspace.py").is_file() or not (source / "operator/server.py").is_file():
        raise ValueError("Receive the complete source root before cumulative installation")
    if output == source or output.is_relative_to(source) or source.is_relative_to(output):
        raise ValueError("Choose an independent receiving directory")
    original = owned_inventory(source)
    source_identity = identity(original)
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if output.exists():
        marker = json.loads((output / RECORD).read_text("utf-8"))
        if marker.get("source_sha256") != source_identity or marker.get("installed_files") != owned_inventory(output):
            raise ValueError("The existing receiving edition has different source; choose its own output directory")
        result = {"state": "current", "application": str(output), "source_sha256": source_identity}
        if archive:
            result["archive"] = archive_application(output, archive)
        return result
    staging = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=".cumulative-application-", dir=output.parent))
    root = staging / "application"
    steps = []
    phase = "copy_source"
    completed = False
    try:
        shutil.copytree(source, root, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(
            "__pycache__", ".git", ".venv", "venv", "node_modules", "*.pyc", "*.pyo", "*.lock"))
        phase = "verify_copied_source"
        if owned_inventory(root) != original:
            raise ValueError("Copied application source differs from its retained inventory")
        sys.path[:0] = [str(root / "operator"), str(root)]
        phase = "compose_application"
        compose(root, steps)
        phase = "restore_original_inputs"
        inputs = restore_inputs(root)
        phase = "check_application_sources"
        validation = check_sources(root)
        if owned_inventory(source) != original:
            raise ValueError("The retained input source changed during installation")
        record = {"schema": "upstate.cumulative-installation/v1", "operation_id": OPERATION,
                  "source_sha256": source_identity, "steps": steps, "restored_inputs": inputs,
                  "validation": validation, "installed_files": owned_inventory(root)}
        write(root / RECORD, json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n")
        phase = "publish_application"
        from source_tools.application_assembly import _rename_directory_new
        _rename_directory_new(root, output)
        completed = True
    except Exception as error:
        details = {"schema": "upstate.cumulative-installation-failure/v1",
                   "operation_id": OPERATION, "state": "error", "phase": phase,
                   "error": type(error).__name__, "message": str(error),
                   "source": str(source), "source_sha256": source_identity,
                   "requested_output": str(output),
                   "retained_stage": str(staging),
                   "retained_application": str(root) if root.is_dir() else None,
                   "completed_steps": steps, "traceback": traceback.format_exc()}
        try:
            retained = owned_inventory(root) if root.is_dir() else {}
            details["changed_files"] = [
                {"path": name, "before": original.get(name), "after": retained.get(name)}
                for name in sorted(original.keys() | retained.keys())
                if original.get(name) != retained.get(name)]
        except Exception as inspection_error:
            details["inventory_error"] = str(inspection_error)
        failure_path = staging / "CUMULATIVE_INSTALLATION_FAILURE.json"
        try:
            write(failure_path, json.dumps(details, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n")
            details["failure_record"] = str(failure_path)
        except Exception as recording_error:
            details["recording_error"] = str(recording_error)
        failure = RuntimeError("Cumulative installation failed; staged source retained at " + str(staging))
        failure.receiving_details = details
        raise failure from error
    finally:
        # A failed attempt keeps its exact partial postimages and original source
        # for diagnosis. Only a successfully published staging directory is removed.
        if completed:
            shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
    result = {"state": "installed", "application": str(output), "source_sha256": source_identity,
              "source_files": len(original), "installed_files": len(record["installed_files"]),
              "validation": validation, "entrypoint": str(output / "operator/server.py")}
    if archive:
        result["archive"] = archive_application(output, archive)
    return result


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--source", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--archive", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        print(json.dumps(install(args.source, args.output, args.archive), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 0
    except Exception as error:
        details = getattr(error, "receiving_details", None)
        if details is None:
            details = {"state": "error", "error": type(error).__name__,
                       "message": str(error), "traceback": traceback.format_exc()}
        print(json.dumps(details, ensure_ascii=False), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Receive observed watershed context in the existing application

This operation receives the complete original Upper Savannah observed hydrology, Eighteenmile study, assessment geography, and published public-water sources into one existing regional scientific Workspace. It uses the maintained source importer, the existing all-87-station assessment mapping code, SpatialReview, SpatialExports, and receiving-water preparation.

## Run the complete operation

From the installed application directory containing model/workspace.py:

```sh
env GDAL_CACHEMAX=16 GDAL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  /ACTUAL/GIS/PYTHON -B -m source_tools.receive_observed_context \
  --workspace /absolute/path/to/existing-regional-workspace \
  --domain-manifest /absolute/path/to/original-domain/sources.json

```

Use the interpreter already installed with the application's GIS and plotting dependencies. The receiver requires the original regional Workspace. It preserves its current sources, profiles, native runs, and reviews.

The original 217-HUC domain is selected by its retained decoded geometry identity. An already imported matching domain is discovered without another domain argument. A successor or other explicitly chosen HUC12 polygon layer can be supplied with repeated --domain-layer-id ACTUAL_LAYER_ID arguments. The receiver requires a selected original domain so the station–watershed result contains the actual spatial joins.

The installed application contains these complete original inputs:

| Source | Manifest | Source records retained |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assessment geography | assessment/geography-model-sources.json | All 87 listed station points in three original CRSs, draft cause and priority facts, original metadata and derivation companions |
| Observed hydrology | observations/observed_hydrology_20261013/model-sources.json | Original gauge inventories, 2020–2025 discharge and stage responses, observed tables, qualifiers, dated nutrient results and original Eighteenmile whole-catchment polygon |
| Eighteenmile lake study | observations/eighteenmile_2023/model-sources.json | Published 2023 study, original laboratory activities and qualifiers, explicitly reconciled chlorophyll cohort, same-date and antecedent flow context |
| Public water | source/water_context/20261012/public-water/sources.public-native.json | Original intake points and four original ARJWS/PRWD published protection polygons |

When the maintained eighteenmile_lake_observation_report.sources.json is installed at the application root, the same receiver also imports its complete original study report and the existing offline interactive lake-observation report. HTML documents open with their native companion paths preserved. Additional editions remain selectable through repeated --context-manifest arguments.

Each manifest remains unchanged. Workspace.import_sources retains every original body and companion by content identity. The assessment manifest includes its original operate_assessment_maps.py as a hash-bound companion, so that file remains byte-for-byte original. The maintained continuation of its mapping code lives separately at source_tools/operate_assessment_context.py.

The receiver accepts --hydrology-manifest, --study-manifest, --assessment-dir and --public-water-dir to use the same complete sources from another retained location. Repeat --context-manifest for additional ordinary source editions such as reported point-source discharge. Repeat --context-layer-id to include an existing native context vector by its actual catalog ID.

## Geographic outputs and original tables

The operation creates the original eight review families:

- Regional assessment and monitoring.
- One view for each of four RFP focus HUC12s.
- Eighteenmile assessment and nutrient context.
- Regional nitrogen and phosphorus listings.
- Original assessment-versus-station HUC source differences.

Every context vector is included in each review whose geographic viewport it intersects. Original point datums remain attached to each layer; the maintained spatial engine projects them into the review's EPSG:5070 view. The native point API inspects every assessment station against each selected original domain. The result retains all original polygon covers, overlapping boundary matches, outside-domain outcomes, field values, and source hashes.

SpatialExports produces its maintained PDF, SVG, PNG, source/provenance, annotation, overlay-feature and map-package outputs. The default is Letter at 150 dpi to keep the first complete receiving operation practical on a shared GIS host. --dpi 220 or --dpi 300 and --paper a4 select the existing alternatives. --skip-export still imports the complete source editions and saves native review selections; running again with print rendering enabled creates that explicitly different operation.

Use --primary-layer-id ACTUAL_BASELINE_LAYER and --comparison-layer-id ACTUAL_ALTERNATIVE_LAYER to open the same geographic context alongside completed native model rasters. --mode difference uses the maintained alternative-minus-baseline path, including its exact grid and units checks.

The same receiving operation also calls the maintained PublishedStudyStore importer on the complete original study directory. It registers the study/version and original observation companions in the existing Published studies desk and records that exact study ID, version ID, collection ID and source counts in receiving.json. Repeated receiving reuses the retained study version.

Tables appear as ordinary Sources entries in the existing operator. Source inspection provides original columns and a 30-row preview. Each source edition exposes the complete original body and all companions for download. The receiver also writes index.html and source-inventory.json with actual CSV row counts, units, declared datums, source URLs, source collection IDs, and direct links to the retained original files.

## Four public-water source areas

The receiver reads the existing receiving-waters.public-spec.json, validates the original typed selectors, imports the current public-water source collection and binds it to the four maintained receptor records. receiving_waters.prepare owns the preparation.

The result retains arjws-swpa-1500, arjws-swpa-200, prwd-swpa-1500 and prwd-swpa-200 in EPSG:26917. All four retain their original source_area relation and polygon geometry. The intake reference remains a separate original point. BUFFER_FT remains the agency's published feet field. The workflow writes scenario-source-areas.json in the maintained format so the existing scenario-analysis desk can select these same geographic source areas.

## Resume and reopen

The exact source manifest hashes, public-water specification, project ID, selected layer IDs and map settings identify the receiving operation. Its output directory is:

```text
workspace/observed-context/<operation-id>/
```

The receiver prints the actual directory and complete result. receiving.json records imports, source-water plan, review IDs, map-pack IDs, counts, completed output hashes and attempt history. A per-operation lock prevents two receivers from running that same selection concurrently.

Run the same command after interruption. Source imports reuse their original content identities. Map saving retains the same scientific selections; the maintained map exporter reuses its complete rendered edition or continues retained rendering. The assessment continuation saves each completed native station inspection and its actual watershed joins under station-checkpoints/. A restarted operation reuses those completed station records and finishes the remaining points.

An operation directory with a different admitted selection is rejected before its progress is altered. Failures after admission retain the exact exception and current progress. The original source data and any completed native map or model result remain in the Workspace.

The existing Workspace backup includes observed-context/ and all retained sources and spatial outputs. Application portability must include the assessment source family alongside observations, model and source_tools. In the restored application, run the same command against the restored Workspace and source manifests; filesystem relocation is excluded from the selection identity.

## Reading the observed context

The source manifests and source inventory preserve numerical and geographic support:

- Discharge is original daily mean flow, with approved/provisional/estimated/revised flags and explicit period completeness. Stage has its separate original gauge reference and units.
- Laboratory concentrations keep original dates, time zones, fractions, depths, analytical methods, detection conditions and limits. Published seasonal statistics and individually reconciled activities retain distinct identities.
- The same-date and antecedent flow companion describes the original upstream Eighteenmile gauge alongside the original lake sampling stations.
- The USGS Eighteenmile polygon is the original upstream whole-catchment basin. The reported gauge drainage area remains the separately recorded denominator used by the hydrology producer.
- The draft assessment HUC labels and the native original-point/polygon joins remain separately inspectable.
- Modeled annual mass rasters retain the maintained model's existing units and cell-area conversion. Receiving this context does not transform observed concentrations into annual loads.

All source URLs, original tables, reproduction programs and retained agency bodies travel with their ordinary source editions.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prepare four published source-water areas in an existing native Workspace.

Inputs are original public SCDES records plus an explicit receptor specification.
The installed application supplies Workspace and the receiving-water GIS engine.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import base64
import copy
import gzip
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys
import tempfile


def read_json(path: Path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))


def save_json(path: Path, value):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    text = json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=path.name + ".", dir=path.parent)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as stream:
            stream.write(text)
        os.replace(temporary, path)
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(temporary):
            os.unlink(temporary)



ORIGINAL_POLYGON_PATH = (
    "source/water_context/20261012/public-water/raw/"
    "scdes-arjws-prwd-source-water-protection-original.json"
)
ORIGINAL_POLYGON_BYTES = 2389556
ORIGINAL_POLYGON_SHA256 = "ddac0feb1c704ca5e95336e21961e08beede1f83b6b820423dffa5a63bd8e285"
CARRIER_LIMIT = 16 * 1024 * 1024


def unique_json_pairs(pairs):
    result = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise ValueError("Duplicate source-carrier JSON key: " + str(key))
        result[key] = value
    return result


def carrier_json(data):
    return json.loads(data.decode("utf-8-sig"), object_pairs_hook=unique_json_pairs)


def limited_gunzip(data):
    with gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data)) as stream:
        result = stream.read(CARRIER_LIMIT + 1)
    if len(result) > CARRIER_LIMIT:
        raise ValueError("Decoded public-water carrier exceeds 16 MiB")
    return result


def decode_original_polygon(carrier: Path):
    """Read the retained original response or its complete published carrier."""
    if carrier.stat().st_size > CARRIER_LIMIT:
        raise ValueError("Public-water carrier exceeds 16 MiB")
    data = carrier.read_bytes()
    if data.startswith(b"\x1f\x8b"):
        data = limited_gunzip(data)
    text = data.decode("utf-8-sig")
    if text.lstrip().startswith("{"):
        value = carrier_json(data)
    else:
        parts = []
        pattern = r"^[ \t]*\x60{3}json[ \t]*\r?\n(.*?)^[ \t]*\x60{3}[ \t]*(?:\r?\n|$)"
        for body in re.findall(pattern, text, flags=re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL):
            item = json.loads(body, object_pairs_hook=unique_json_pairs)
            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("schema") == "upstate.application-source-part/v1":
                parts.append(item)
        if not parts:
            raise ValueError("The original public-water source parts were not found")
        first = parts[0]
        count = first.get("parts")
        if type(count) is not int or not 1 <= count <= 128 or len(parts) != count:
            raise ValueError("The original public-water source part inventory is incomplete")
        if any(type(part.get("part")) is not int for part in parts):
            raise ValueError("Invalid original public-water source part number")
        parts.sort(key=lambda part: part["part"])
        if [part["part"] for part in parts] != list(range(1, count + 1)):
            raise ValueError("Missing or duplicate original public-water source part")
        fields = (
            "schema", "edition", "parts", "encoding", "payload_bytes",
            "payload_sha256", "compressed_bytes", "compressed_sha256",
        )
        if any(any(part.get(key) != first.get(key) for key in fields) for part in parts):
            raise ValueError("Public-water source parts belong to different carriers")
        if first.get("encoding") != "gzip+base64":
            raise ValueError("Unsupported original public-water source encoding")
        for field in ("compressed_bytes", "payload_bytes"):
            if type(first.get(field)) is not int or not 0 < first[field] <= CARRIER_LIMIT:
                raise ValueError("Invalid public-water carrier size: " + field)
        compressed = base64.b64decode("".join(part["data"] for part in parts), validate=True)
        if (len(compressed) != first["compressed_bytes"]
                or hashlib.sha256(compressed).hexdigest() != first["compressed_sha256"]):
            raise ValueError("Original public-water compressed carrier identity differs")
        data = limited_gunzip(compressed)
        if (len(data) != first["payload_bytes"]
                or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != first["payload_sha256"]):
            raise ValueError("Original public-water source carrier identity differs")
        value = carrier_json(data)
    if isinstance(value, dict) and value.get("schema") == "commons.source-bank/v1":
        files = value.get("files")
        if not isinstance(files, list) or len(files) != 1:
            raise ValueError("Use the one-file original public-water geometry bank")
        entry = files[0]
        if (not isinstance(entry, dict) or entry.get("path") != ORIGINAL_POLYGON_PATH
                or entry.get("bytes") != ORIGINAL_POLYGON_BYTES
                or entry.get("sha256") != ORIGINAL_POLYGON_SHA256
                or not isinstance(entry.get("content"), str)):
            raise ValueError("The geometry bank is not the original public-water source")
        data = entry["content"].encode("utf-8")
    elif not isinstance(value, dict) or not isinstance(value.get("features"), list):
        raise ValueError("Use the original public-water response or its retained geometry bank")
    if (len(data) != ORIGINAL_POLYGON_BYTES
            or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != ORIGINAL_POLYGON_SHA256):
        raise ValueError("Original public-water polygon byte identity differs")
    return data


def receive_original_polygon(carrier: Path, source_dir: Path):
    """Retain exact original bytes; reuse an identical received source."""
    body = decode_original_polygon(carrier)
    destination = source_dir / "raw" / Path(ORIGINAL_POLYGON_PATH).name
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if destination.is_symlink():
        raise ValueError("Original public-water destination must be a regular file")
    reused = destination.exists()
    if reused:
        if not destination.is_file() or destination.read_bytes() != body:
            raise ValueError("Existing public-water source differs: " + str(destination))
    else:
        fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".public-water-original-", dir=destination.parent)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
                stream.write(body)
                stream.flush()
                os.fsync(stream.fileno())
            try:
                os.link(temporary, destination)
            except FileExistsError:
                if destination.is_symlink() or not destination.is_file() or destination.read_bytes() != body:
                    raise ValueError("Concurrent public-water source differs: " + str(destination))
                reused = True
        finally:
            os.unlink(temporary)
        directory_fd = os.open(destination.parent, os.O_RDONLY)
        try:
            os.fsync(directory_fd)
        finally:
            os.close(directory_fd)
    return {
        "carrier": str(carrier),
        "path": str(destination),
        "bytes": len(body),
        "sha256": ORIGINAL_POLYGON_SHA256,
        "reused": reused,
    }



def validate_original_selection(source_dir: Path, receptors):
    path = source_dir / "raw" / Path(ORIGINAL_POLYGON_PATH).name
    body = path.read_bytes()
    if (len(body) != ORIGINAL_POLYGON_BYTES
            or hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest() != ORIGINAL_POLYGON_SHA256):
        raise ValueError("Prepared public-water input is not the retained original polygon response")
    original = carrier_json(body)
    reference = original.get("spatialReference", {})
    if (reference.get("latestWkid") or reference.get("wkid")) != 26917:
        raise ValueError("Original public-water geometry must retain EPSG:26917")
    features = original.get("features", [])
    if len(features) != 4 or {feature.get("attributes", {}).get("OBJECTID") for feature in features} != {11, 12, 131, 132}:
        raise ValueError("Original public-water geometry must retain all four published records")
    selected = set()
    for receptor in receptors:
        selector = receptor["source"]
        where = selector.get("where")
        if (selector.get("source_id") != "scdes-arjws-prwd-swpa-20261012"
                or not isinstance(where, dict)
                or set(where) != {"OBJECTID", "INTAKE", "BUFFER_FT"}):
            raise ValueError("Use each original typed public-water record selector")
        matches = [
            feature for feature in features
            if all(type(feature["attributes"].get(key)) is type(value)
                   and feature["attributes"].get(key) == value
                   for key, value in where.items())
        ]
        if len(matches) != 1:
            raise ValueError("Public-water receptor does not select one original typed record: " + receptor["id"])
        selected.add(matches[0]["attributes"]["OBJECTID"])
    if selected != {11, 12, 131, 132}:
        raise ValueError("Public-water receptors must preserve the four distinct original records")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--model-root", required=True, type=Path,
                        help="Existing application directory containing model/workspace.py.")
    parser.add_argument("--workspace", required=True, type=Path,
                        help="Existing native Workspace to receive the original sources.")
    parser.add_argument("--source-dir", type=Path,
                        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] /
                        "source/water_context/20261012/public-water")
    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--geometry-carrier", type=Path,
                        help="Original polygon JSON or the complete retained 26-part Markdown carrier.")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    model_root = args.model_root.resolve()
    source_dir = args.source_dir.resolve()
    output = args.out.resolve()
    if not (model_root / "model/workspace.py").is_file():
        parser.error("--model-root must contain the installed model/workspace.py.")
    manifest_path = source_dir / "sources.public-native.json"
    spec = copy.deepcopy(read_json(source_dir / "receiving-waters.public-spec.json"))
    expected = {"arjws-swpa-1500", "arjws-swpa-200",
                "prwd-swpa-1500", "prwd-swpa-200"}
    receptors = spec.get("receptors", [])
    if len(receptors) != 4 or {item.get("id") for item in receptors} != expected:
        raise ValueError("The public source-water specification must contain its four distinct receptors.")
    if spec.get("analysis_crs") != "EPSG:26917":
        raise ValueError("The source-area operation uses the original EPSG:26917 analytical CRS.")
    for receptor in receptors:
        if receptor.get("relation", {}).get("method") != "source_area":
            raise ValueError("Use the published polygon through the source_area relation.")
        if receptor.get("source", {}).get("source_collection_id") is not None:
            raise ValueError("The input specification must bind to this actual native import.")

    received_geometry = None
    if args.geometry_carrier is not None:
        received_geometry = receive_original_polygon(args.geometry_carrier.resolve(strict=True), source_dir)
    validate_original_selection(source_dir, receptors)

    sys.path.insert(0, str(model_root))
    from model.workspace import Workspace
    from model.receiving_waters import prepare

    workspace = Workspace(args.workspace.resolve(), create=False)
    # The importer checks original byte hashes, including both metadata companions.
    collection = workspace.import_sources(str(manifest_path))
    entries = {entry["id"]: entry for entry in collection["entries"]}
    required_sources = {"scdes-public-surface-intakes-20261012",
                        "scdes-arjws-prwd-swpa-20261012"}
    if not required_sources.issubset(entries):
        raise ValueError("Native import did not retain the required original sources.")
    for receptor in receptors:
        receptor["source"]["source_collection_id"] = collection["id"]
        receptor["metadata"]["intake_reference"]["source_collection_id"] = collection["id"]
    save_json(output / "receiving-waters-spec.json", spec)
    plan = prepare(workspace, spec)
    outcome = {
        "schema": "upstate.public-water-preparation/v1",
        "workspace": str(workspace.root),
        "application_root": str(model_root),
        "python_version": sys.version.split()[0],
        "source_collection_id": collection["id"],
        "original_protection_sha256": entries["scdes-arjws-prwd-swpa-20261012"]["body"]["sha256"],
        "plan_id": plan["id"],
        "plan_state": plan["state"],
        "analysis_crs": spec["analysis_crs"],
        "receptor_ids": [item["id"] for item in receptors],
        "source_records": [
            {
                "id": source_id,
                "uri": entries[source_id]["uri"],
                "sha256": entries[source_id]["body"]["sha256"],
                "bytes": entries[source_id]["body"]["bytes"],
                "features": entries[source_id]["features"],
            }
            for source_id in sorted(required_sources)
        ],
        "native_manifest": str(manifest_path),
        "native_selection": str(output / "receiving-waters-spec.json"),
    }
    if received_geometry is not None:
        outcome["received_original_geometry"] = received_geometry
    # Retain the exact source-area choices for the existing scenario analysis desk.
    # Model totals remain clipped to that desk's selected baseline reporting area.
    zones = []
    for receptor in receptors:
        metadata = copy.deepcopy(receptor.get("metadata", {}))
        metadata.update({
            "source_plan_id": plan["id"],
            "receptor_ids": [receptor["id"]],
            "source_relation_method": receptor["relation"]["method"],
            "source_geometry_scope": "published_polygon",
            "source_classification": copy.deepcopy(receptor.get("classification", {})),
        })
        zones.append({
            **copy.deepcopy(receptor["source"]),
            "id": receptor["id"],
            "title": receptor["title"],
            "map_family": receptor["family"],
            "metadata": metadata,
        })
    source_areas_path = output / "scenario-source-areas.json"
    source_areas = {
        "schema": "upstate.scenario-source-areas/v1",
        "selection": {
            "title": "Published source-water planning areas",
            "zones": zones,
        },
        "origin": {
            "source_plan_id": plan["id"],
            "workspace": str(workspace.root),
            "analysis_crs": spec["analysis_crs"],
            "source_collection_id": collection["id"],
            "original_protection_sha256": outcome["original_protection_sha256"],
            "source_records": copy.deepcopy(outcome["source_records"]),
            "native_preparation": str(output / "public-water-preparation.json"),
            "native_selection": str(output / "receiving-waters-spec.json"),
        },
    }
    save_json(source_areas_path, source_areas)
    outcome["native_source_areas"] = str(source_areas_path)
    save_json(output / "public-water-preparation.json", outcome)

## Interpretation

All counts use pixel centres. `joint_valid_cells` requires finite nonnegative K and a finite non-NoData value from the original NLCD raster. `joint_valid_pct` uses selected in-grid cells as its denominator. `outside_grid_area_m2` separately exposes polygon area omitted by the raster extent.

`land_k_unresolved_cells` counts valid NLCD cells other than open water that lack usable K. `nlcd_nodata_cells` reports missing or nonfinite land cover separately. `water_k_zero_cells` counts actual code-11 water pixels whose final K is zero. The original preparation counts retained in the summary identify the source-wide native-rating and explicit water-policy contributions. Per-HUC K statistics use the final physical SI raster values and finite nonnegative pixels. A zero is a value; NoData remains missing.

Regional totals are measured from union geometries, so shared HUC boundaries are not summed twice. Optional reporting totals use the original reporting polygon. The buffer-wide totals include the upstream and model-edge area needed by the source operation.

### Raster flags

Flags combine by bitwise OR; outside the buffered domain is zero.

| Bit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Inside the actual buffered model domain |
| 2 | K is finite and nonnegative |
| 4 | K is source NoData |
| 8 | K has data but is negative or nonfinite |
| 16 | Original NLCD has a finite non-NoData value |
| 32 | Original NLCD value is 11, open water |
| 64 | Inside the selected original reporting geometry and model domain |

For example, a valid land cell normally has value 19 (1 + 2 + 16), and an unresolved land cell has value 21 (1 + 4 + 16). Add 64 when it also falls in the selected reporting polygon. Use bitwise operations for map styling because multiple conditions coexist.

## Source and method

The geometry phase creates geographic SDA AOIs from each target tile's geographic bounds, including a one-pixel halo. The halo protects the target pixel centres during coordinate transformation. The target raster windows themselves are disjoint on the selected NLCD grid.

Each geographic AOI is queried for its native polygon count, complete polygon-ID set and exact selected geometry pages. The interpretation phase collects the actual unique mapunit keys from those polygons and submits batches of at most 1,000 keys to SDA's native mapunit-list AOI interface. It obtains the actual interpretation catalog, short-form defaults and long-form XML, then sends the original short-form JSON unchanged to `getrating`. Native metadata, original rating columns and legend are retained from the returned interpretation ID. This avoids rerunning the same mapunit interpretation for every geometry tile.

The geographic and mapunit-list AOIs have different jobs: geographic AOIs provide clipped geometry; mapunit-list AOIs provide the native soil interpretation. USDA documents that geometric AOI tables are populated only for the geographic form. The code follows those original interfaces directly.

Regional source-catalog observations bracket the capture. Every actually used soil survey must retain the same native survey row and spatial version. Individual HTTP receipts preserve the observed response interval.

## Native choice values

USDA declares both the original and effective datatype of `chorizon.kwfact` as **Choice**. Its actual whole-soil result carries values such as `.20` in `MapUnitRatingString`; `MapUnitRatingNumeric` is empty for this native rule. The importer parses the original choice with Decimal, checks its exact label and colour against the same interpretation's source legend, and retains the original string beside the numerical projection. It never fills or relabels the original numeric column. A missing choice stays missing.

The retained October 12 Anderson County calculation used all **34** native mapunits from SC007, original AOI **13217298** and interpretation **109629**. It returned **32** rated mapunits and **2** missing choices. Those original responses remain available in the source packet; a continued importer consumes their existing result IDs. Metadata and rating tables use the provider's actual `AoiID` field. The provider's `LayerOption` is **Surface Layer**; its separate `HorizonAggregationMethod` metadata remains **Weighted Average**, alongside the unchanged short-form layer choice and full ParameterXml.

Run from the complete product root using the already-equipped native GIS Python. Select the original numeric NLCD raster and the retained full upstream-domain vector used for DEM/grid preparation.


Supply the actual source layer or filter through `--layer` and `--where-json` where needed. The buffer must equal the explicit native model selection. Source and output paths are selected by the existing native worker; the command does not start another compute service.

The selected source directory retains each complete response and reuses its original bytes on continuation. `--resume` allows the same incomplete public-source request to continue after a transport interruption or eligible temporary HTTP failure. # Original Southeast annual reference targets

This workflow receives the complete original nitrogen, phosphorus and sediment calibration tables published in the USGS Southeast SPARROW mapper, joins their published COMIDs to that same service's original river network, and admits selected annual targets into the existing Upper Savannah Workspace. It uses the existing catchment validator, observation importer, calibration selection and residual-map workflow.

## What the observations mean

The source is USGS release [10.5066/P9A682GW](https://doi.org/10.5066/P9A682GW), documented by its complete original FGDC XML. The mapper is the publisher's Southeast service, identified as “Republished with 10.06.2019 data update -ESM”. The source package retains the entire original service definition, layer 42 network definition, original calibration query responses and all reach-query responses. Original bytes have SHA256 and byte-length pins in `FILES`.

| Source | Original table | Reference field | Units admitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total nitrogen, 00600 | layer 37, 598 rows | ACTUAL | kg/year |
| Total phosphorus, 00665 | layer 36, 589 rows | ACTUAL | kg/year |
| Suspended sediment, 80154 | layer 39,CONSTITUEN=SUSPSED | ACTUAL_MT | metric_tonnes/year |
| Total suspended solids, 00530 | layer 39,CONSTITUEN=TSS | ACTUAL_MT | metric_tonnes/year |

Layer39 contains 395 rows across its two original constituents. `PLOAD_TOTA` and `PLOAD_MT` remain in the retained original attributes as regional SPARROW predictions. They never become observed/reference loads. The source's `TSS_CONV` is a regional model term, retained unchanged; this workflow does not apply it to the original calibration targets or convert a TSS series into SSC.

The XML explicitly gives the global model calibration-target horizon as 1999-10-01 through 2014-09-30. The annual CSV stores 1999-10-01 inclusive and 2014-10-01 exclusive, with `temporal_basis.scope="source_global"`. That is the published shared target horizon. The mapper does not expose each individual station's sampling window or final estimator selector. A target is one long-term annual mass rate, not fifteen separate yearly observations, and it is never multiplied by the fifteen-year horizon.

The regional targets describe 2012 reference conditions. Their source-era land cover and climate remain distinct from current native scenario inputs. Comparability notes survive in the original observation record and should explain the intended historical-versus-current comparison. The source provides no target standard error in these mapper tables; `uncertainty.value` is null. SPARROW prediction errors cannot fill that gap. The existing published-SE sensitivity workflow therefore identifies these source rows as uncovered.

## Published reach attribution and current basin geometry

Every source target retains its literal original station identifier and COMID. Combined records such as `comb600_6269342` and `comb665_6269342` remain separate source identities. A current numeric USGS station identifier is not substituted.

The original mapper's layer 42 provides the published-network `REACHCODE` for each calibration COMID. Its first eight digits supply HUC8. The retained crosswalk covers all 665 unique COMIDs across the complete three calibration tables, so the seven Upper Savannah HUC filter is an exact source-network selection rather than a coordinate box or station-name guess.

Current NLDI basins are a distinct geometry edition. A selected published COMID must resolve to its actual current NLDI feature and full upstream basin. Their complete raw responses, URLs, byte lengths and hashes are retained. This does not assume that the regional publisher's revised network and current NLDI routing are identical.

The maintained `usgs_annual._retained_catchment` checks the actual NLDI identifier, response URLs, CRS, valid polygon components and intersection with the source feature. It computes area from ellipsoidal geometry, preserves every original component, and requires a specific explanation for any explicitly omitted component. The helper updates the catchment context to the correct regional release DOI and retains the original publisher-network attribution. One original series is selected per catchment/native pollutant; TSS and SSC cannot both occupy the same sediment objective unit.

# USGS annual reference import

This source tool takes the published annual estimates in [USGS release 10.5066/F7DN436B](https://doi.org/10.5066/F7DN436B) through original archive receiving, station selection, upstream geometry, ordinary Workspace import and the installed calibration catalog.

## Original release and estimator

The publisher's original dictionary is retained in the source directory. It defines four original output members: total nitrogen 00600, total phosphorus 00665, suspended sediment 80154 and total suspended solids 00530. Each water-quality station has its own original final-method field.

| Original selector | Selected annual value | Selected published standard error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| beale | rload_a_XXXXX | serload_a_XXXXX |
| flux5pkd | LOAD_A_XXXXX | SLOAD_A_XXXXX |

The tool reads that field exactly. Values are already kilograms per year. Fluxmaster supplies a detrended long-term mean for the 2012 reference; Beale supplies its published long-term mean. The original water-quality and flow periods, station identifiers, paired flow station, COMID, sample/censor counts, merged-station text and both estimator columns remain in the retained source row.

The included flow-data start and end dates define the source comparison period. The original last included calendar day becomes an exclusive end by adding one day. The mean annual rate is preserved; it is not multiplied by the length of the source period. The imported metadata supplies the appropriate whole-year or elapsed-day weighting for the existing calibration selection.

Suspended sediment and total suspended solids keep separate original constituent identities. Select one original series for any one upstream catchment/native sediment comparison. Their scientific relationship to the native hillslope-export prediction remains visible with the source row and the selection's comparability note.

# Eighteenmile Creek original stream nutrients

This complete source package joins four South Carolina stream monitoring stations to their original WQP nutrient results and the retained NLDI whole-reach basin for USGS-02186702. It supplies the existing observed-context and Published studies workflow with original concentrations, detection limits, dates, sampling activities, source locations and executable coverage tables.

## Original source and coverage

The two complementary publisher date queries contain **589 result rows across 153 activities**, spanning 6 January 2020 through 4 December 2025. Their inclusive query windows are 2020–2022 and 2023–2025. All 63 original CSV fields remain unchanged. The source manifest pins every original URL, byte count and SHA256.

| Original stream station | Results | Activities | Source coverage |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| SV-233 | 263 | 68 | 2020-01-06 through 2025-11-04 |
| SV-245 | 4 | 1 | 2023-12-14 |
| SV-375 | 185 | 48 | 2022-01-11 through 2025-12-04 |
| SV-376 | 137 | 36 | 2023-01-23 through 2025-12-04 |

The original nutrient characteristics are ammonia (124 rows), nitrate + nitrite (153), Kjeldahl nitrogen (153), phosphorus (153), and nitrogen (6). There are 408 numeric results in mg/L and 181 entries marked `Present Below Quantification Limit`. Each censored entry retains its exact original limit value, limit type and limit unit. A blank measured value remains blank.

Six original `Nitrogen` rows are labeled `Calculated` and have method name `Total Nitrogen`. Each is lower than its same-activity nitrate + nitrite value; two equal the paired numeric Kjeldahl result, and four equal its reporting limit. The normalized `result_type`, method and activity IDs preserve this source inconsistency for the maintained component-consistency analysis. Source values remain unchanged.

The original Seneca station query contains 47 locations: 20 streams and 27 lakes. This package selects the four actual Eighteenmile stream identifiers explicitly; the lake locations retain their separate study/source relationship.

## Geography

All four original WGS84 station points lie within the full-resolution NLDI **whole-reach** basin retained by the existing hydrology source. This is an actual point-in-original-polygon calculation using its 480-vertex exterior ring. The executable supports Polygon and MultiPolygon components, holes and an explicit boundary result.

The original query uses `splitCatchment=false`. USGS documents that a split catchment instead places the local basin boundary at the feature's linear-reference position: [original basin semantics](https://api.water.usgs.gov/docs/nldi/basin/). The `full_reach_basin_relation` column refers to that exact whole-reach source. Preserve this distinction when matching observations to the flow gauge, particularly SV-233 south of the gauge's reported location.

The normalizer also accepts a retained `original/eighteenmile-gauge-basin.geojson` member declared in `source-manifest.json`. When that precise publisher response is supplied, it adds a separate `gauge_split_basin_relation` column. The maintained native acquisition request is in the original project thread at message 1791864567.609429.

## Reproduce and use the source

Run in any existing Node environment:

```sh
node derive-nutrients.mjs SOURCE_DIRECTORY OUTPUT_DIRECTORY
```

The command verifies every manifest original before deriving:

- `derived/nutrient-results.csv`: all 589 records with exact source-file/CSV-record references, original measured and limit values, fractions, statuses, method IDs, dates, clocks and time zones.
- `derived/station-basin-join.csv`: four original station identities, locations, periods and whole-reach spatial relations.
- `derived/station-year-characteristic-coverage.csv`: counts by actual station, year, characteristic and sample fraction, retaining quantitation limits and analytical methods.
- `derived/source-summary.json`: complete source counts and the spatial/normalization method.

The published outputs were produced by this complete deterministic derivation from the pinned originals. Its CSV parser preserves quoted commas, embedded newlines and escaped quotes. Output order uses ordinal string comparison.

For the existing observed-context source inventory, retain this full directory beside the original daily-flow source. Join by exact station ID and sampling date and keep source fractions, analytical methods, actual coverage and censoring visible. Nitrogen, Kjeldahl nitrogen and nitrate + nitrite retain their original characteristic identities; any later combined quantity belongs to a separately recorded calculation. Existing native load estimation consumes the actual source observations, selected gauge relationship, source periods and retained flow series.

The complete all-years original query response is also retained on the [engineering source page](https://app.notion.com/p/3f7dd77231008147bfb0d97e296fda3b); the two unchanged date-query files here make the full record set directly readable and reproducible.

def recipe(manifest, source_path, title, kind, support, columns, *,
           constants=None, dimensions=(), interpretation="", **extra):
    return {"manifest": manifest, "path": source_path, "title": title,
            "observation_kind": kind, "time_support": support,
            "columns": columns, "constants": constants or {},
            "series_dimensions": list(dimensions), "interpretation": interpretation, **extra}

def recipes():

        recipe(HYDROLOGY, "derived/daily_stage.csv",
               "Savannah gauges: original daily mean stage",
               "receiving_water_stage", "daily_mean",

                "period_start": "date", "qualifier": "qualifiers", "method": "method_id"},

        recipe(HYDROLOGY, "derived/nutrient_activity_total_nitrogen.csv",
               "Eighteenmile routine activities: derived total nitrogen",
               "receiving_water_derived_concentration", "original_sample",
               {"station_id": "monitoring_location_id", "value": "quantified_tn_mg_l",
                "period_start": "sample_date", "method": "method"},

               interpretation="Source processor combines same-activity TKN and NOx. This view selects its fully quantified concentration; original component IDs, censor bounds, and same-date gauge context remain in the rows. Blank quantified values remain blank.")

def selected_sources(root, manifest_names):
    result = {}
    for name in manifest_names:
        path = (root / name).resolve(strict=True)
        manifest = read_json(path)
        if manifest.get("schema") != "upstate.sources/v1":
            raise ValueError("Select an ordinary retained scientific source manifest: " + str(path))
        index = {}
        for entry in manifest["entries"]:
            source_path = entry["path"]
            if source_path in index:
                raise ValueError("A source manifest has ambiguous table paths")
            index[source_path] = entry
        result[name] = (path, index)
    return result

def import_context(workspace, source_root, manifest_names, output):
    root = Path(source_root).resolve(strict=True)
    desired = [r for r in recipes() if r["manifest"] in manifest_names]
    if not desired:
        raise ValueError("Choose at least one maintained observation source manifest")
    sources = selected_sources(root, manifest_names)
    # Preflight every selected table before copying or creating an observation edition.
    for item in desired:
        path, entries = sources[item["manifest"]]
        entry = entries.get(item["path"])
        if not entry or entry.get("kind") != "table":
            raise ValueError("The selected source edition lacks table " + item["path"])
        body = (path.parent / entry["path"]).resolve(strict=True)
        if not body.is_relative_to(path.parent.resolve()):
            raise ValueError("The original table is outside its retained manifest")
        if hashlib.sha256(body.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != entry["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("The original table differs from its source hash")
        with body.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as stream:
            headers = next(csv.reader(stream), [])
        required = [item["columns"].get(k, k) for k in ("parameter", "value", "unit")
                    if k not in item["constants"]]
        if len(headers) != len(set(headers)) or set(required) - set(headers):
            raise ValueError("The original table lacks the selected value columns: " + item["path"])
    ws = Workspace(workspace)
    collections = {name: ws.import_sources(path) for name, (path, _) in sources.items()}
    imported = []
    for item in desired:
        source = sources[item["manifest"]][1][item["path"]]
        collection = collections[item["manifest"]]
        body, entry = ws.source_file(collection["id"], source["id"])
        metadata = {key: value for key, value in item.items()
                    if key not in ("manifest", "path")}
        metadata.update({
            "schema": "upstate.observed-source-context/v1",
            "value_basis": "context", "source_uri": source["uri"],
            "sha256": entry["body"]["sha256"],
            "source_collection_id": collection["id"], "source_id": source["id"],
            "source_manifest_sha256": hashlib.sha256(sources[item["manifest"]][0].read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
            "source_table_path": item["path"], "source_vintage": source["vintage"],
            "source_records": {"source_id": source["id"], "source_sha256": source["sha256"],
                               "selection": "All original rows retained unchanged"},
        })
        edition = ws.import_observations(body, metadata)
        if edition["admitted_count"]:
            raise RuntimeError("Context intake unexpectedly admitted annual model loads")
        imported.append({"id": edition["id"], "title": metadata["title"],
                         "source_collection_id": collection["id"],
                         "source_id": source["id"], "sha256": metadata["sha256"],
                         "rows": len(edition["rows"]),
                         "context_count": edition["context_count"],
                         "admitted_count": edition["admitted_count"],
                         "observation_kind": metadata["observation_kind"]})
    result = {"schema": "upstate.observed-context-import/v1",
              "workspace": str(ws.root.resolve()), "project_id": ws.project.get("id"),
              "sources": {name: value["id"] for name, value in collections.items()},
              "observations": imported}
    atomic_json(Path(output), result)
    return result

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--workspace", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--source-root", required=True,
                        help="Directory containing the original observations/ tree")
    parser.add_argument("--manifest", action="append", choices=[STUDY, HYDROLOGY, EFFLUENT],
                        help="Select one or repeat; default imports available maintained editions")
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    root = Path(args.source_root).resolve(strict=True)
    names = list(dict.fromkeys(args.manifest or
                             [name for name in (STUDY, HYDROLOGY, EFFLUENT) if (root/name).is_file()]))
    result = import_context(args.workspace, root, names, args.output)
    print(json.dumps({"workspace": result["workspace"],
                      "observation_editions": len(result["observations"]),
                      "observation_rows": sum(item["rows"] for item in result["observations"]),
                      "receipt": str(Path(args.output).resolve())}, sort_keys=True))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Apply the observed-context additions without replacing shared application files."""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()

def patch_text(body, edits, name):
    for edit in edits:
        old, new = edit["old"], edit["next"]
        if body.count(new) == 1 and not body.replace(new, "", 1).count(old):
            continue
        candidates = [candidate for candidate in [old] + edit.get("previous", [])
                      if body.count(candidate) == 1]
        if len(candidates) != 1:
            raise ValueError("Current " + name + " does not have the unique maintained seam: " + edit["label"])
        body = body.replace(candidates[0], new, 1)
    return body

def add_static_asset(body):
    tree = ast.parse(body)
    candidates = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if (isinstance(node, ast.Compare) and isinstance(node.left, ast.Name)
                and node.left.id == "selected" and len(node.ops) == 1
                and isinstance(node.ops[0], ast.NotIn)
                and len(node.comparators) == 1):
            # Current host composes its original literal assets with extension assets.
            for selected in ast.walk(node.comparators[0]):
                if not isinstance(selected, ast.Set):
                    continue
                if all(isinstance(x, ast.Constant) and isinstance(x.value, str) for x in selected.elts):
                    values = [x.value for x in selected.elts]
                    if {"index.html", "app.mjs", "spatial.mjs"}.issubset(values):
                        candidates.append((selected, values))
    if len(candidates) != 1:
        raise ValueError("Select the maintained operator's unique static-asset allowlist")
    node, values = candidates[0]
    if "observed_series.mjs" in values:
        return body
    # AST column offsets are UTF-8 byte offsets; preserve the rest of the current host exactly.
    lines = body.encode("utf-8").splitlines(keepends=True)
    first = sum(len(line) for line in lines[:node.lineno-1]) + node.col_offset
    last = sum(len(line) for line in lines[:node.end_lineno-1]) + node.end_col_offset
    addition = "{" + ", ".join(repr(x) for x in values + ["observed_series.mjs"]) + "}"
    raw = body.encode("utf-8")
    return (raw[:first] + addition.encode("utf-8") + raw[last:]).decode("utf-8")

def atomic(path, raw):
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=path.parent, prefix=".observed-context-", delete=False) as stream:
        pending = Path(stream.name)
        stream.write(raw)
        stream.flush()
        os.fsync(stream.fileno())
    os.chmod(pending, path.stat().st_mode & 0o777)
    os.replace(pending, path)
    fd = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
    try:
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)

def install(application, receipt):
    root = Path(application).resolve(strict=True)
    patch_path = root / "source/observed_context_patch.json"
    patch = json.loads(patch_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if patch.get("schema") != "upstate.observed-context-patch/v1":
        raise ValueError("Choose the original observed-context component")
    changes = []
    for name, edits in patch["edits"].items():
        path = root / name
        original = path.read_bytes()
        current = original.decode("utf-8")
        updated = patch_text(current, edits, name)
        if name.endswith(".py"):
            ast.parse(updated, filename=name)
        changes.append((path, original, updated.encode("utf-8")))
    path = root / "operator/server.py"
    original = path.read_bytes()
    updated = add_static_asset(original.decode("utf-8")).encode("utf-8")
    ast.parse(updated.decode("utf-8"), filename=str(path))
    changes.append((path, original, updated))
    for name, expected in patch["additions"].items():
        path = root / name
        body = path.read_bytes()
        if sha(body) != expected["sha256"] or len(body) != expected["bytes"]:
            raise ValueError("The received complete component differs: " + name)
        if name.endswith(".py"):
            ast.parse(body.decode("utf-8"), filename=name)
    # Every source seam and complete added file has now passed preflight.
    backup = root / "source/observed-context-originals"
    backup.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    results = []
    for path, original, updated in changes:
        if path.read_bytes() != original:
            raise ValueError("The shared application changed during component preflight")
        before, after = sha(original), sha(updated)
        name = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
        if original != updated:
            retained = backup / before
            if retained.exists() and retained.read_bytes() != original:
                raise ValueError("The retained original application source differs")
            if not retained.exists():
                with retained.open("xb") as stream:
                    stream.write(original)
                    stream.flush()
                    os.fsync(stream.fileno())
            atomic(path, updated)
        results.append({"path": name, "before_sha256": before, "sha256": after,
                        "bytes": len(updated), "changed": original != updated})
    result = {"schema": "upstate.observed-context-install/v1",
              "application": str(root), "patch_sha256": sha(patch_path.read_bytes()),
              "files": results}
    destination = Path(receipt)
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    destination.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
    return result

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--application", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
    parser.add_argument("--receipt", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    install(args.application, args.receipt)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Dated measurements in the existing observation desk

This component connects the actual retained scientific sources to the existing Observed water quality desk. It adds a station/parameter/date plot, original-row CSV and SVG downloads, and a repeatable native import command. It preserves the current original-row search, annual-load comparison, asynchronous CSV/source-method selection guards, extension assets and all other application code.

## Existing application integration

The source was composed against merged PR2807 head 22130c9cffb89e52c70097aeabc06692725ddb0f. The actual model/observations.py is 23,618 bytes and unchanged from the maintained source; the actual app.mjs has the newer CSV race-condition repair. The installer modifies the exact ingest function, eleven narrow app seams and only the literal static-asset set inside the current server's extension union. It retains the original source bodies by SHA256. The complete Workspace, model, delivery, portable and server implementations remain the current application's versions.

Apply this additive component through the current application's existing source assembler or receive its five complete files under the application root. Then:

python source/install_observed_context.py --application /actual/application --receipt /actual/receipts/observed-context-install.json

All maintained seams and new file hashes are checked before writes. Repeating this command retains already-applied changes. The actual pre/post hashes go into its receipt. An unexpected modified seam reports its exact label so the current implementation can be composed deliberately. It never substitutes an old whole application file.

Restart the existing operator process after the source change, preserving its configured Workspace, authentication and port. This makes the Python ingest change active in its existing server. Reloading the browser then loads observed_series.mjs from the same static-asset route.

## Import the actual retained source editions

Use the same application interpreter and populated Workspace. The source root contains the original observations/ tree, including each selected manifest and its retained bodies.

python -m source.import_observed_context --workspace /actual/populated-workspace --source-root /actual/scientific-source-root --output /actual/receipts/observed-context-import.json

By default the programme selects the maintained study, hydrology and effluent-flow manifests present under that tree. A specific source can be selected with --manifest, repeated as needed:

- observations/eighteenmile_2023/model-sources.json
- observations/observed_hydrology_20261013/model-sources.json
- observations/eighteenmile_2023/npdes/flow_context/model-sources.json

The receiver also recognizes the exact earlier component hashes and upgrades that owned edition atomically with retained originals. The ingest patch accepts either the original maintained function or the component's earlier complete function.

The complete current study is in Slack F0C8JNNS1BP; the actual hydrology and monthly effluent-flow companions are in F0C8QAH0AQ2. The current study's source-bound detection classification successor is compatible: the importer reads the selected manifest's actual hash rather than hard-coding an older derived-table hash.

The programme first checks every selected table/header/hash. It imports each ordinary upstate.sources/v1 edition through Workspace.import_sources, opens its hash-bound native body through Workspace.source_file, and calls the existing Workspace.import_observations. Metadata binds source collection, original table ID/hash, manifest hash, original URI and vintage. All original CSV cells and row order remain available. The output receipt contains the actual populated Workspace path, collection IDs, observation IDs, kinds, counts and hashes. Identical sources and metadata produce the same immutable observation IDs.

## Scientific interpretation

The study intake retains all 920 original normalized results. Parameter, physical unit, fraction, sample depth and project define separate series. Dates and source clocks/timezones remain original. A non-detect is displayed at its stated bound with an open downward triangle; an above-range result uses an open upward triangle. These symbols represent censor bounds, not substituted measurements. Four original E. coli upper-quantitation-limit records are explicitly handled even in the earlier normalized edition that labeled them quantified. The remaining 676 numerical results and 240 lower bounds preserve their original values and units.

USGS daily discharge retains 33,459 actual daily means across the selected gauges. Stage and dated monthly-flow summaries are separate observation editions. Daily traces connect only consecutive original dates; missing dates break the trace. Monthly summaries retain valid/expected days, approval status and original measured volume. Blank censored or otherwise unquantified original context values retain their source status without being labeled a numeric validation failure; annual-load validation remains strict. The original detection condition and stated bound also appear in the record table. Their original hydrology period_end is inclusive; context metadata preserves that convention when displaying duration. DMR period_end_exclusive remains exclusive. The annual model-comparison period contract is unchanged. Gauge selection prevents mixing station datums or different drainage areas. The derived routine total-nitrogen view uses the source processor's fully quantified same-activity TKN + NOx result, retaining the components and censor intervals in original rows.

The monthly DMR component exposes separate fields from the same unmodified original tables:

- quantified reported amounts with actual partial coverage;
- complete source amounts only where the source processor marks the month/cohort complete;
- gross reported source mass divided by observed gauge volume;
- reported effluent volume as a fraction of observed gauge volume.

Each view retains its original reporting features, monitoring location, pollutant species, dates, coverage days, gauge relation and source-period JSON. The gross mass/volume index is a source-term calculation in mg/L; it does not become a receiving-water concentration measurement. The complete same-period gauge series remains separately selectable.

All these editions have value_basis=context. The annual model-comparison admission rules still require an explicit original annualization method, annual mass units, positive complete period, accepted qualifier and catchment ID. Ordinary context no longer requires a fictional catchment ID or annual interval. Explicit context constants only supply genuine table-wide parameter/unit labels; original cells remain unchanged.

## Operator use

Open Observed water quality, choose the retained edition, then select its parameter/unit/source group and station. Optional date filters restrict the displayed original rows. The existing record search remains immediately below the dated plot. Download selected original rows exports their actual CSV fields; Download dated plot exports the same monochrome SVG with source dates, units and point tooltips.

The importer can create fourteen distinct value views when all three complete source editions are installed. Several DMR views deliberately share the same retained original rows while selecting different physically defined output columns. The receipt reports observation rows per view, not a claim of additional independent measurements.

## Verification and native receiving

The current full patched browser module and added module were parsed in the JS runtime; the eleven app edits were applied twice against the actual current source and remained unchanged on the second pass. Every one of the 920 actual WQP rows reaches the date/value renderer: 676 reported values, 240 original lower bounds and four original upper bounds in 33 parameter/unit/depth/project groups. The model's existing comparison tail remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

The installed Python programmes must run on the equipped native application. Return the real install receipt, import receipt, existing operator Workspace ID/path, one actual censored E. coli plot and one actual USGS daily-series SVG. Use the current authenticated browser to verify source selection and source downloads in the already-populated application. These are direct receiving checks on the actual sources.
